en: For you, O Agni, were the first inventor of this prayer, the wondrous invoker;
O bull, you have made your power invincible, so that it may prevail against all opposing force.
Then you sat down as the Hotṛ, the more excellent sacrificer, at the place of libation, seeking nourishment, worthy of praise;
toward you, the first one, the men seeking the gods and striving for great wealth have followed.
As if moving through a crowd with many riches, those who are watchful have followed after you for wealth—
the radiant Agni, beautiful to behold, vast, full of fatness, and shining forevermore.
Seeking glory, they have attained unimpaired glory by approaching with reverence the station of the god;
they have even assumed names worthy of sacrifice, and they rejoice in your auspicious appearance.
The people on earth increase you; both kinds of wealth of men belong to you.
You are known as the savior in the crossing over, and you are forever the father and mother of human beings.
Worthy of honor, beloved among the people, the joyous Agni has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest, the most skilled in sacrifice.
As such, we, bowing ourselves, would sit near you who shine within our home, with reverence.
As such, O Agni, we, the pure-minded seekers of the gods, implore you, the new one, for our welfare.
You, O Agni, shining with the great light of heaven, have led the people.
The sage of the people, the lord of the eternal tribes, the subduer, the bull among men; Agni, who seeks the advance of prayers, the impeller, the purifier, the ruler, the worshipful one of riches.

O Agni, that mortal has sacrificed and performed his labor who has attained your gift of oblations through fuel; he who understands the offering with prostrations, protected by you, gains all desirable things.
To you, that great one, we shall offer worship with great reverence, O Agni, with fuel and oblations;
on the altar, O Son of Strength, with songs and hymns, may we strive to abide in your auspicious favor.

O Agni, you who have spread across the two worlds with your radiance and with glories— you, the seeker of renown and the deliverer— shine forth for us even more widely with great, enduring, and abundant strengths.
O Vasu, grant us evermore the wealth of men; bestow abundant cattle upon our children and progeny.
Grant us many great and sinless refreshments; may auspicious glories of high renown be ours.
O King Agni, through my devotion to you, may I obtain many treasures in manifold ways by means of your wealth-giving power.
For many treasures, O Agni, rich in boons, are indeed found within you; they belong to you, the King, for the one who serves you.
For you, O Agni, possess lordly glory like Mitra;
O Vasu, you who are active among all people, you nourish renown like prosperity.
For indeed, the peoples invoke you with sacrifices and with songs;
to you the prize-winning steed, free from malice, traversing the mid-air, moves—he who belongs to all people.
In unison, the men of heaven kindle you, the banner of the sacrifice,
when this human folk, seeking favor, invokes you at the rite.
The mortal who exerts himself with prayer for you, the Bounteous Giver, shall prosper;
through the aid of the Great Heaven, he crosses over his enemies as if over distress.
The mortal who, with fuel, attains your oblation and sharpening power,
O Agni— he prospers in a dwelling rich in offspring and lasting a hundred years.
Your brilliant smoke rises up, bright and extended across the sky; for like the sun in its splendor, O purifier, you shine with your radiant form.
For thus you are to be praised among the people, our beloved guest;
delightful like an aged house, and worthy of protection like a son.
For by your power, O Agni, you are anointed in the wooden vessel like a prize-winning steed;
like the self-dependent one who wanders around, like a swift horse, you are the child who is never to be held back.
O Agni, you [consume] even those things that are unshakable, like a beast in a pasture;
for when your eternal powers, O skillful one, cut down the forests.
For you, O Agni, go as the Hotṛ-priest in the house of the people who perform the sacrifice;
O Lord of the People, bring us prosperity and graciously accept the oblation, O Aṅgiras.
O God, Agni, whose greatness is like that of Mitra, call hither to us the gods and the favor of Heaven and Earth.
Seek out well-being and a secure dwelling from the men of heaven; may we cross over our enemies, over distresses, and over misfortunes—may we cross them by your protection.
O Agni, he who protects the cosmic order (*ṛta*) and is born of the cosmic order shall dwell in peace; seeking the gods, he attains your wide light.
O God, that mortal whom you, Varuṇa, in harmony with Mitra, protect from distress by casting it away.
He has sacrificed with sacrifices, he has labored with ritual services, and he has bestowed gifts upon Agni, whose doors are successful.
Even so, neither the disfavour of the glorious ones nor distress, nor arrogance, reaches that mortal man.
Like the sun, whose appearance is stainless, when your terrifying thought comes upon the one who is burning with fervor;
like the booty of a neighing steed, this dwelling of the forest-born one is delightful at any time of night.
Even though his form is sharp, his appearance is great; with his mouth he devours like a horse controlled by the bridle.
His tongue flickers like an axe; burning, he consumes the wood like a swift consumer.
Like an archer about to shoot, he aims; he sharpens his brilliance like the edge of iron.
With wondrous course, he is the chariot-pole who, like a bird alighting on a tree, speeds with the flight of a swift-winged bird through the night.
Like a singer, he clothes himself in the rays of dawn; great as Mitra, he calls aloud with his flame—He who is ruddy by night and by day for men, the immortal one, ruddy by day for men.
Like the roar of heaven when it releases its rain, the bull has bellowed; he has roared among the plants.
Like one driven by fervor, moving with rapid flight, he has filled the two worlds, the well-wedded pair, with wealth.
He who, with his nourishing and worthy hymns, has flashed like lightning with his own vital powers;
or he who, like R̥bhu, fashioned the host of the Maruts—he, the brilliant and impetuous, has shone forth.
Just as you, O Hotṛ, son of strength, perform sacrifice with offerings for the gods at the assembly of men,
so today, O Agni, desiring them, sacrifice to the willing gods for us who are likewise willing and equal.
May that Agni, the radiant illuminator, like the eye of the dawn, grant us delight— he who is worthy of praise and to be known,
the immortal one who possesses all life among mortals, the guest who awakens at daybreak, Jātavedas.
Whose majesty the heavens admire like the sun, who clothes himself in splendors bright as the radiant sun;
he, the ageless and purifying one, drives far away even the ancient works of Aśna.
For you, O Son, are a speaker; Agni, seated at the feast, has by his very birth made for himself a path and food.
As such, O winner of strength, bestow strength upon us; like a king, may we dwell in safety within a domain free from wolves.
He who sharpens his horns and eats the obstructing food, like Vāyu the sovereign, passes through the nights;
may we overcome those who oppose your commands, as a swift horse avoids falling pitfalls.
Like Sūrya with his radiant rays, O Agni, you have spread through both worlds with your light;
brilliant and anointed with flame, he leads us beyond the darkness, flying like the son of Uśij in his flight.
For we have chosen you, the most delightful one, with the flames of our hymns; hear our great prayer, O Agni!
Like Indra, no deity fills you with power, nor do the most heroic men satisfy you with their bounty like Vāyu.
Now, O Agni, lead us by paths of well-being with those who are free from harm; bring us across distress and grant wealth.
Bestow that favor upon our patrons and upon the singer; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
I invoke for you the Son of Strength, the youth, whose speech is guileless, the youngest one with our prayers;
he who, being wise, impels riches containing all boons, the one of many desires who is free from deceit.
In you, O many-faced Hotṛ, the worshipful ones have placed their treasures at evening and at dawn;
in you, the purifier, they have gathered all blessings and all beings, as if upon the broad earth.
From of old you have sat among these people; by your wisdom, you became the charioteer of desirable things.
Therefore, O wise Jātavedas, you bestow riches in succession upon the one who serves you.

O Agni, whoever from afar seeks to harm us, or whoever, great as Mitra, would plot against us from within— with your own ageless, bull-like flames, O most scorching one, burn him down with your heat, you who are full of fervor.
O Son of Strength, that mortal who honors you with sacrifice, with fuel, with hymns, and with songs— he, O Immortal One, being wise among mortals, shines forth with wealth, splendor, and renown.
O Agni, do that quickly as you are impelled; being powerful, drive away our rivals with your might.
Since you are praised with words throughout the days, take pleasure in this; let the singer’s prayer resound.
May we attain that desire of ours through your protection, O Agni; may we attain wealth, O Lord of Wealth, with noble heroes.
May we, seeking booty, attain booty; may we attain your undecaying and ageless splendor.
Seeking a path by means of sacrifice with a new hymn, he approaches the Son of Strength;
the Hotṛ goes toward the divine one who cuts down the forest, whose path is black, who is radiant, and who is invited for the feast.
White-shining, thundering, dwelling in the realm of light, most youthful with his unaging, roaring flames— Agni, the purifier, who most frequently devours many broad things as he follows after them.
O pure Agni, your pure flames, impelled by the wind, move forth in every direction;
they are fiercely consuming, divine, and ever-active, boldly felling the forests as they break them down.
O Radiant One, those bright and pure steeds of yours, when let loose, shave the earth;
then your whirling flame shines far and wide, sweeping across the ridges of the dappled earth.

Then the tongue of the bull, who fights for cattle, darts forth like a released thunderbolt; like the snare of a hero, the devouring flame of Agni, difficult to resist and terrible, consumes the forests.
With the radiance of your great impeller, you have boldly spread across the terrestrial expanses.
As such, drive away all fears with your powers; contending against rivals, consume those who seek to harm us.
O Wondrous One, bestow upon us wondrous wealth—wonderful, most marvelous, a giver of vitality, with wondrous dominion;
O Radiant One, grant to the singer radiant, vast riches consisting of many heroes, through your radiant rays.
The gods have generated from their mouth Agni Vaiśvānara— the head of heaven, the messenger of earth, born of the Eternal Order (ṛta)—
the sage, the sovereign, the guest of men, as a vessel for their mouths.
They have cried out together toward him, the navel of sacrifices, the seat of riches, the great reservoir;
the gods have generated Vaiśvānara, the charioteer of rites, the banner of sacrifice.
From you, O Agni, the inspired singer is born as a victor; from you come heroes who overcome the enemy.
O Vaiśvānara, O King, bestow upon us desirable riches.
O Immortal Vaiśvānara, when you were being born, all the gods celebrated you together like a newborn child;
through your mental powers they attained immortality when you shone forth from your two parents.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, no one has dared to violate those great ordinances of yours, when,
being born in the lap of your parents, you discovered the banner of light within the appointed courses of the days.
By the sight of Vaiśvānara and by the signal of the immortal heaven, his ridges have been measured out.
Upon his head, indeed, all beings have grown like branches; seven streams have sprung forth.
He of skillful wisdom who measured out the realms, Vaiśvānara, the sage who [measured] the luminous spheres of heaven—
he who has spread himself around all beings, the undeceived guardian, the protector of immortality.
Now I shall proclaim the power of the nourishing, virile, ruddy one; I shall proclaim the sacrificial assemblies of Jātavedas.
A new, pure hymn flows for Vaiśvānara like the beautiful Soma; it purifies itself as a lovely offering for Agni.

Being born in the highest heaven, Agni, the guardian of vows, protected the sacred ordinances. With his skillful wisdom, Vaiśvānara measured out the mid-air and touched the firmament with his greatness.
The wondrous Mitra propped apart the two worlds; he drove away the darkness with light within the space between them.
Vaiśvānara rolled out the two bowls like two skins and assumed all manly vigor.
In the lap of the waters, the mighty ones seized him; the clans stood near the King who is worthy of praise.
As a messenger from afar, Mātariśvan brought Agni Vaiśvānara from the dwelling of Vivasvat.
In age after age, O Agni, bestow upon those who praise you a wealth worthy of the assembly, most glorious and ever new.
O King, undecaying one, as with a sharp blade, strike down the evildoer with your splendor, as one fells a tree.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, maintain for us among our patrons an unaging dominion and excellent heroic power; may we, through your protections, O Agni, win booty in hundreds and thousands.
O thou who dwellest in the three places, protect our patrons with thy unfailing guardians, O thou who art desired;
and guard the host of us who give, O Agni Vaiśvānara, and, being praised, prolong our lives.
The black day and the bright day revolve by means of the known regions;
as soon as he is born, Agni Vaiśvānara, like a king, has driven away the darkness with his light.
I do not understand the warp nor the woof, nor that which they weave while striving together in the contest.
Who indeed, being a son here, can speak of things beyond his father who stands below?

He alone knows the warp and he knows the woof; he shall speak the words that ought to be spoken in due season—he who, as the guardian of immortality, perceives this, moving below while looking beyond another.
This is the first Hotṛ; behold him! This immortal light among mortals—this one has been born, firmly seated, the immortal one increasing in body.
A firm light has been established for all to behold—the mind, the swiftest among those that fly within. All the gods, of one mind and one purpose, move rightly toward this single will.
My two ears flutter; my sight flutters; this light that was placed within my heart flutters.
My mind wanders, its thoughts directed far away: what indeed shall I speak? And what now shall I imagine?
All the gods, trembling with fear, paid homage to you, O Agni, as you stood in the darkness. May Vaiśvānara protect us for our aid; may the Immortal protect us for our aid.
Place before you at the commencement of the sacrifice, during the rite, the delightful, celestial Agni with this well-fashioned hymn;
for he, our radiant Jātavedas, shall make our sacrifices successful through our praises.
O brilliant Agni, of many aspects, kindled by the fires of Manu, O Hotṛ—
just as one honors him with a hymn, so do our thoughts flow pure like clarified butter as strength for him.

He has flourished among mortals with glory—he, the inspired singer, who has given gifts to Agni with hymns. To him, the one of wondrous luster, he grants various aids for the winning of the stall rich in cattle.
He who, at his birth, filled the two wide worlds, whose path is black with far-reaching luster;
even through the thick darkness of the night, that purifier has become visible with his flame.
Now, O Agni, bestow upon us a wondrous wealth with many powers, and upon our patrons—
those who surpass all other people by their bounty, their fame, and their heroic deeds.
O Agni, graciously accept this sacrifice which the worshipper, desiring you, offers while sitting before you with oblations.
Among the Bharadvājas, you have accepted the well-fashioned hymn for the winning of prize-winning booty that is to be seized.
Drive away our enemies, increase our nourishment; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
Sacrifice, O Hotṛ, being impelled as the most skilled sacrificer; O Agni, drive away the oppressors as if by the instigation of the Maruts.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, the Nāsatyas, Heaven and Earth, turn hither for our sacrifice.
You, O god, are our most delightful and guileless Hotṛ-priest, dwelling among mortals at the assemblies.
O Agni, as the bearer [of oblations], with your purifying tongue and mouth, sacrifice to your own self.
For even the blessed prayer yearns for you, so that the singer may worship the gods at the sacrifice;
when the most inspired of the Aṅgirases, the sage, the seer, utters the honeyed hymn at the rite.
He has shone forth, the self-purifying, far-illuminating Agni; perform the sacrifice to the two wide-reaching worlds, O Agni.
Him whom the five tribes, offering oblations with reverence, anoint like Āyu—the one who is rich in nourishment.
When I trim the sacrificial grass with reverence for Agni, the ladle is offered, filled with ghee and well-prepared;
the dwelling-place has been fixed upon the seat of the earth, and the sacrifice has taken its stand like the eye in the sun.
O Agni of many aspects, being kindled with the gods and with the fires, grant us your favor, O Son of Strength; clothed in wealth, may we pass beyond distress as if across a narrow pass.
In the midst of the dwelling, the Hotṛ, the king upon the sacrificial grass—Agni, the impeller, shall worship both worlds.
This son of strength, the observer of cosmic order, has spread himself from afar like Sūrya with his brilliance.
O King, worthy of sacrifice, you who are well-disposed toward us, in whom Heaven herself, as it were, has offered worship for the sake of total prosperity;
you who abide in the three stations, like the stride of one who has crossed over, come to sacrifice the offerings and the riches of men.

Whose impetus is most brilliant, the sovereign of the woods, he has shone forth like a driver increasing on his path. Like a guileless runner, the immortal one, irresistible among the plants, takes heed of himself.
May Agni Jātavedas be praised in our home with our impetuous songs like swift steeds;
winning the wood with his power, like a racer, he has been brought to old age by sacrifices, like a father for his son.
Now they admire his splendors when he hews them out at will and follows along the broad earth—
he who, as soon as released, rushes forward with greater speed than a thief fleeing from debt, crossing the desert wastes like a sovereign.
As such, O courser Agni, being kindled with all thy fires, protect us from reproach;
bring us wealth, drive away misfortune, and may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
From you, O blessed Agni, all blessings spread forth like the branches of a tree;
through your readiness to hear, there comes wealth, strength in the conquest of Vṛtra, rain from heaven, and the flow of waters—O you who are worthy of praise.
You are Bhaga for us, for you grant wealth; like one who travels all around, you rule with wondrous luster.
O Agni, like Mitra, you are the steward of the great *ṛta* and of abundant beauty, O God.
He, the true lord, slays Vṛtra with his might; O Agni, the inspired singer brings away the wealth of the Pani.
O wise one, born of Truth, you who are in harmony with the Son of Waters, you urge him on with riches.

O Son of Strength, that mortal who, through songs, hymns, and sacrifices, has attained sharpening for you in the sacred knowledge—O God Agni, he gains every desirable thing; he possesses grain and rules over all riches.
O Agni, Son of Strength, grant those men glory and heroic sons so that they may prosper;
for with your power you provide abundant nourishment for cattle against the ravenous wolf and the enemy.
O eloquent Son of Strength, O far-reaching Agni, grant us offspring and descendants who possess vigor.
Through all our songs of praise, may we attain fulfillment; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
The mortal who, through his prayers and meditations, has taken pleasure in the service of Agni—
may he, enjoying it, choose for himself abundant food as protection from of old.
For Agni indeed is the wise one; Agni is the most skillful seer.
At the sacrifices, the human clans invoke Agni as the Hotṛ-priest.
For, O Agni, the wealthy Aryas vie with one another for your protection;
the Āyus, overcoming the Dasyu, strive by means of their sacred rites to subdue the lawless.
Agni bestows a hero who wins the waters, who overcomes the assailants, and who is the lord of the good;
at the mere sight of whose power his enemies tremble with fear.
For Agni, by his wisdom, the god protects the mortal from reproach;
he is the victorious one whose wealth is unassailable, whose riches are unassailable in the contests for booty.

O Agni, great as Mitra, call hither to us the gods, O god; proclaim our good will to heaven and earth. Seek out well-being and a secure dwelling from the men of heaven. May we cross over hatreds, distresses, and difficulties; may we cross them, may we cross them by your protection.
I strive with my song toward this guest of yours, who awakens at dawn, the lord of all people;
he comes from heaven by his very birth, pure in every way, and as an embryo he eats even that which is eternal for a long time.

Like a well-placed friend whom the Bhr̥gus established in the tree— the one worthy of praise, with upward-flaming radiance— so you, O wondrous one, being well-pleased at the sacrifice of Vītahavya, are magnified day by day with hymns of praise.
As such, be the harmless increaser of Dakṣa’s skill, the subduer of the enemy, whether distant or near.
O Son of Strength, bestow upon mortals wealth and wide protection for Vītahavya; grant wide protection to Bharadvāja.
I strive toward you—the radiant guest, the celestial hero, Agni the invoker of men, the performer of the fair sacrifice;
like a sage whose speech dwells in heaven, the divine bearer of oblations, the steward, with my well-fashioned hymns.
He who, with his purifying and observant grace, has shone upon the earth like the radiance of the dawn;
he who, like a swift steed on its course, rejoices in battle, and who, ageless, hastens like one parched by heat.
Worship Agni after Agni with your fuel; praise your beloved guest, each one most dear.
Invite the Immortal hither with your songs, for as a god among the gods, he wins what is desirable; for as a god among the gods, he accepts our service.
I praise with song the kindled Agni, the pure purifier, steadfast at the front of the sacrifice;
the inspired priest, the invoker, the one of many boons, the guileless sage—Jātavedas—we implore him for his favors.
Thee, O Agni, the immortal messenger, the bearer of oblations, the protector worthy of praise, they have established in age after age;
both gods and mortals have seated thee with homage—the watchful, all-pervading lord of the people.
Adorning both worlds according to their laws, O Agni, you traverse the two realms as the messenger of the gods.
Since we choose your devotion and your favor, therefore be auspicious to us, providing triple protection.
Him, the fair-faced, beautiful to behold, swift-moving, the one more wise than the ignorant—let us serve.
May he, knowing all ways, perform the sacrifice; may Agni announce our offering among the immortals.

O Agni, you protect that man and you deliver him who has brought a prayer to you, the Seer, O Hero—whether it be the sharpening of the sacrifice or its completion; him indeed you satisfy with strength and with wealth.
O Agni, protect us from the one who seeks to harm us; O powerful one, guard us from reproach.
May your smoke-enveloped path reach toward us, and may desirable, thousandfold wealth come to us.
Agni is the Hotṛ, the lord of the house, the king; he, Jātavedas, knows all births.
He who is the best sacrificer among both gods and mortals—may he, the observer of Truth, perform the sacrifice.
O Agni, O Hotṛ of the sacrifice, O purifier with your bright luster, come today to the people, for you are the sacrificer.
You shall worship according to the Truth as you expand in your greatness; carry the oblations that are yours today, O youngest one.
Behold the well-prepared offerings; may one establish you between the two worlds to worship.
O Maghavan Agni, help us in the winning of booty; may we cross over all difficulties, may we cross them, may we cross them with your protection.

O Agni, O god of beautiful countenance, together with all the gods, sit first upon this wool-softened seat. Lead the sacrifice, nest-like and rich in ghee, straight to Savitṛ for the sake of the sacrificer.
The wise ones churn this very Agni, as Atharvan did,
whom they brought forth unerring from the dark-hued [plants], even as he was eager to leap forward.
Be born for the feast of the gods, for complete success and for well-being!
Bring hither the immortal gods who increase the Truth; let the sacrifice reach the gods.
O Agni, Lord of the House of men, we have made thee great with fuel;
may our household duties not be deficient, and sharpen us with thy keen splendor.
O Agni, you have been appointed as the Hotṛ-priest of all sacrifices among the human race, together with the gods.
With your delightful tongues, do you, the great one, sacrifice for us at the rite; bring the gods here and worship them.
For you, O wise one, know directly the ways and the paths to the gods at the sacrifices, O Agni of noble intellect.
I invoke you, as did Bharata with his prize-winning steeds, for prosperity; he sacrificed at the sacrifices to you, the one worthy of sacrifice.
You [bestowed] these many desirable things upon Divodāsa, who presses the soma,
and upon Bharadvāja, the donor.
As an immortal messenger, bring hither the divine folk,
listening to the excellent praise of the sage.
O Agni, mortals with devoted minds invoke you, the god, at the sacrifices for the banquet of the gods.
I worship your appearance and your will, O bounteous one;
may all who desire it take pleasure in them.
You are the Hotṛ priest, appointed by Manu; you are the bearer of oblations, most wise in speech. O Agni, sacrifice to the clans of heaven.
O Agni, come for the feast, being praised for the giving of the oblation;
sit down as the Hotṛ-priest upon the sacred grass.
O Aṅgiras, we strengthen you with fuel-sticks and with clarified butter; shine forth brightly, O youngest one!
O God Agni, you win for us that vast and glorious wealth, and great heroic power.
O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the lotus;
the priest churned you from the head of the universe.
And him, O Agni, the seer Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, kindled—
the slayer of Vṛtra, the shatterer of forts.
The bull Pāthya has kindled you, the greatest slayer of Dasyus,
the winner of wealth in every battle.
Come here, O Agni; indeed, I shall speak these other songs to you.
May you grow strong by means of these drops.
Wherever you set your mind upon a higher skill,
there you shall make your dwelling.
For no one has ever surpassed your bounty, O Vasu, among those who bestow gifts; therefore, you shall accept our worship.
Agni, the descendant of Bharata, the slayer of Vṛtra, the one of many insights, has come—
the true lord of Divodāsa.
For he, by his greatness, bestows wealth that surpasses all earthly things; winning it, he is unassailed and unconquered.
O Agni, as in the past, with new and enduring glory,
you have spread far and wide with your great radiance.
O friends, boldly offer a hymn and a sacrifice to your Agni; sing and chant for the Ordainer.
For he, possessing the wisdom of a seer, sat down as the Hotṛ-priest throughout the ages of mankind,
acting as the messenger and the bearer of the oblations.
O Vasu, worship those two kings, the Ādityas of pure vows, the host of Maruts,
and the two worlds, Rodasī, here.
O Agni, son of strength, your appearance is auspicious for the mortal who seeks nourishment; you are the offspring of immortality.
May he who seeks you with skillful thought, bestowing the finest gifts and possessing excellent splendor, this mortal man, today attain the well-fashioned hymn.
These [men] of yours, O Agni, protected by you, seeking nourishment for their whole span of life,
overcome the hostilities of the enemy, subduing the hostilities of the enemy.
May Agni with his sharp flame strike down every devouring demon;
may Agni win wealth for us.
O Jātavedas, you who move among all people, bring us wealth accompanied by brave sons; O you of noble power, destroy the demons.
O Jātavedas, protect us from distress and from the one who intends evil; guard us, O Sage, with your sacred power.
O Agni, whatever mortal of evil intent offers us up to slaughter,
protect us from that distress.
O God, with your tongue drive away that evildoer— the mortal who seeks to slay us.
O victorious Agni, grant extensive protection to Bharadvāja; bestow upon him excellent wealth.
May Agni, seeking wealth, strike down the Vṛtras through inspired praise— Agni who is kindled,
bright, and invoked with oblations.
In the womb of his mother, the father of his father, flashing forth in the imperishable,
he sits within the seat of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
O Jātavedas, you who are far-seeing, bring us a prayer that wins progeny,
O Agni, which shall shine in heaven.
O Agni, son of strength, we who offer nourishing food have poured forth our songs toward you, whose appearance is delightful.
We have come to your protection as if to the shade from the heat;
O Agni, you who shine like gold.
O Agni, like a fierce archer or a sharp-horned bull, you have shattered the fortresses.
Him whom they carry in their hands like a ring, like a newborn infant— the Agni of the people, the performer of the perfect sacrifice.
Bring forth the god, the best finder of wealth, for the feast of the gods;
let him sit down in his own place of origin.
Sharpen this beloved guest who has been born in Jātavedas; settle him, the master of the house, upon his pleasant seat.
O Agni, yoke those horses of yours, O God, which are well-trained; they carry you readily according to your will.
Come toward us; bring [the gods] hither to enjoy the offerings, so that the gods may come for the drinking of the Soma.
O Agni of the Bharatas, rise up with brilliant, unceasing light; blaze forth and shine out, O ageless one!

The mortal who, with an offering, seeks to win over the god Agni at the sacrifice, and who, with outstretched hands, invokes the Hotṛ priest—the true sacrificer of heaven and earth—with reverence; Please provide the final answer. I am ready to assist you with your request. To proceed effectively, could you please provide the text you would like me to translate? I will provide the translation as requested once I have the source material.
O Agni, we bring to you with a hymn an oblation fashioned by the heart;
may these become for you bulls, stallions, and even barren cows.
The gods kindle Agni, the foremost, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra,
by whom wealth has been brought hither and the demonic powers shattered, O powerful one.
Drink the Soma, O fierce Indra, which you, being praised, have struck down as you burst open the great stall of cattle—
O bold one, wielder of the thunderbolt, who with your powers have slain Vṛtra and all hostile forces.
Drink this, O Indra— you who are the consumer of the *ṛjīṣa*, the overcomer, the one with beautiful jaws, the bull among prayers, the breaker of the cow-pens,
the wielder of the thunderbolt, and the one who stands upon the two bay horses— pierce through to wondrous spoils of war!
Drink thus; as of old, let it exhilarate you. Hear our prayer and grow strong through our songs.
Make the sun manifest; cause the food to swell. Slay the enemies, O Indra, and pierce through for the cattle.
O Indra, self-sustained one, these exhilarating draughts, once drunk, have made you, the radiant one, swell greatly;
they have gladdened you—the great, perfect, powerful, and pervasive lord of victory.

Exhilarated by those [Soma drops], O Indra, you caused the sun and the dawn to shine forth, rending asunder the firm fortresses; you shook the great mountain from its own unshakable seat, releasing the cows that were held within.
By your wisdom and by your wondrous deeds, you have placed the cooked within the raw through your power;
you threw open the doors for the ruddy cows and, acting as a friend to the Aṅgirases, released the cattle from the firm enclosure.
You have filled the broad earth, O Indra of great wondrous power; lofty and vast, you have propped up the high heaven.
You have supported the two worlds, whose sons are the gods—the ancient, youthful Mothers of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
Then all the gods, O Indra, placed you alone, the powerful one, at the front for the battle;
when the godless one challenged the gods, they chose Indra there in the struggle for the light of heaven.
Then even the heaven itself trembled at your thunderbolt, twice over, out of fear of its own wrath—
when Indra, possessing all life, struck down the dragon as he lay there, mocking him with his arrogance.

Then, O fierce one, Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for you that great thunderbolt with a thousand spikes and a hundred edges— a weapon according to your desire, irresistible, with which, O drinker of the soma-residue, you crushed the roaring dragon.
May all the Maruts, acting in harmony, strengthen him for whom you, O Indra, have cooked a hundred buffaloes.
Pūṣan and Viṣṇu poured out three lakes for him: the Vṛtra-slaying, intoxicating stalk.
You released the great, encompassed flood of the rivers, the wave of the waters that stood obstructed.
Along their downward course, O Indra, you opened the path; you sent the active waters rushing down to the ocean.

May this new prayer turn toward you for protection— toward Indra, who has performed all these deeds, the great, the fierce, the undecaying, the giver of victory, the one with excellent heroes, well-armed, and wielder of the good thunderbolt.
O Indra, bestow upon us inspired singers glory, strength, nourishment, and radiant wealth for the sake of victory;
O Indra, grant heroic patrons to Bharadvāja, and be mindful of us on the decisive day.
Through this [hymn], may we win god-appointed booty; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
Praise him, the much-invoked Indra, who possesses surpassing power, who conquers and is unassailed. With these songs, strengthen the fierce bull of the peoples, the irresistible subduer.

He is the warrior, the hero, the stirrer of battle, the one who shares the spoils, the great smiter, roaring like a bull, the drinker of the dregs; raising a vast cloud of dust, the shaker of human races, he alone has become the conqueror of the peoples.
You indeed, O Indra, alone didst devour those Dasyus and protect the Aryan people.
Is this heroic deed of yours truly yours, O Indra, or is it not? Declare it according to the truth.
Truly, I acknowledge that power of yours, O most mighty one born with strength; it belongs to you, the swiftest of the swift.
That fierce power of the fierce, the most powerful of the strong, has become the conqueror of the weak, for you are the subduer of the feeble.
May that ancient friendship of ours be with you, O wonder-worker, together with the Aṅgirases who spoke thus.
You, the shaker of the unshakable, struck down Vala as he was fleeing; you shattered all his fortresses and threw open his gates.

For he, the fierce one, is to be invoked with prayers; acting as a sovereign lord in the great battle against Vṛtra, he, the wielder of the thunderbolt, has become one who is to be sought for the winning of offspring and progeny in the midst of conflicts.

By his greatness, he has extended beyond the generations of men with his immortal name. He is united with splendor, with power, with wealth, and with heroic might—he who is most manly among those who dwell together.
He who does not falter, he whose person is never false, he of auspicious name— Indra shattered Cumuri and Dhuni,
Pipru, Śambara, and Śuṣṇa, for the destruction of their fortresses and for their eternal prostration.
O Indra, mount your chariot for the slaying of Vṛtra with your exalted and most praiseworthy power;
take the thunderbolt in your right hand and, O giver of many gifts, strike down the magical illusions.

Like Agni with his weapon, O Indra, burn down the Rakṣas as if it were dry forest; like a terrible thunderbolt, he who with deep and lofty [power] has shattered [the obstacles], driven away misfortunes, and subdued them.
O Indra of many glories, come hither by a thousand paths with wealth and abundant strength;
O Son of Strength, O Much-invoked One, you over whom no godless one has ever held power to ward you off.
The greatness of the ancient, fiercely impetuous one of abundant splendor has overflowed beyond heaven and earth.
He has no enemy, no counterpart, and no firm foundation; he is the conqueror of many wiles.
May that deed of yours performed today be manifest: that you for him [Indra] struck down Kutsa, Āyu, and Atithigva.
You have firmly fixed many thousands upon the earth; with boldness, you have carried Tūrvayāṇa across.
Then, O God, all the gods rejoiced after you, the wisest among the wise,
when you, being praised, created wide space for the oppressed heaven, for the people, and for your own self.
Heaven and Earth have yielded to this might of yours, O Indra; the immortal gods have submitted.
O Accomplisher, perform that which remains undone for you; through sacrifices, bring forth a new hymn of praise.

Great is Indra, manly, filling the people; moreover, doubly vast and undiminished in his powers, he has grown strong for our sake, a hero. Broad and wide, he has been made well-fashioned by the makers.
The prayer has placed Indra alone for the sake of gain— the great, lofty, undecaying, and youthful one—
who has increased by invincible power, he who has grown instantly and completely.
Widen your arms and extend your hands; bestow upon us glories.
Like a domestic herdsman tending his cattle to the herd, O Indra, turn toward us in battle.
We who seek strength now invoke here that Indra of yours, the one who observes with his powers,
so that the singers of old may be like him— blameless, faultless, and unharmed.
Firm in his vows, giver of wealth, increased by Soma, he indeed possesses much desirable property.
Paths of riches meet in him, like rivers flowing together into the ocean.
O most powerful hero, bring us the mightiest strength, the most potent force that overcomes all;
bring to us, O Lord of the Bay Horses, all the splendors and manly powers of men, so that we may rejoice.

O Indra, bring us that exhilarating draught of yours which conquers armies and is never-failing, which has grown exceedingly strong— by means of which, aided by you, we may think ourselves victorious when winning offspring and progeny.
O Indra, bring to us manly vigor that wins the prize, ever-increasing and most skillful—
that by which, through your protections, we may overcome our enemies in battles, whether they be kin or strangers.
O Bull, let your fierce strength come from behind, from above, from below, and from the front;
let it come hither from every side. O Indra, bestow upon us the splendor that shines like the sun.
O Indra, most manly one, may we win desirable wealth through our glorious deeds with your manly aids;
for you, O King, behold the treasure of both worlds: bestow upon us a great, firm, and lofty jewel.

We invoke here for our new protection that Indra— the bull accompanied by the Maruts, the ever-increasing, the one whose enemies are not deficient, the divine ruler, the all-conquering, the fierce giver of victory.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, subject even the people who consider themselves great to these men for whom I am;
therefore, we invoke you on earth in the struggle for heroes, for progeny, for cattle, and for waters.
O much-invoked one, through these friendships of yours may we prevail over every enemy;
O hero, slaying both kinds of obstacles, may we, protected by you, rejoice in abundant wealth.
Like the sky, O Indra, that wealth which stands over men in battles through its power—
O Son of Strength, grant us that which brings thousands, wins the fertile fields, and overcomes the Vritras.
Like that of heaven, all sovereign power was established for you by the gods, O Indra;
when, O consumer of the Soma dregs, acting in concert with Viṣṇu, you slew Vṛtra, the dragon who had obstructed the waters.
Triumphant, more powerful than the strong, and mightier than the mighty, Indra— whose greatness has increased through the performed *brahman*—
became the king of the honeyed Soma, when he aided the shatterer of all the fortresses.
By the hundreds, the Paṇis fled there at Indra’s hands, for the sake of the ten-fingered sage in the winning of the light.
With his weapons, he overthrew the illusions of the insatiable Śuṣṇa; he did not leave even a trace behind, as if devouring food.
All life was taken from the great deceiver when Śuṣṇa fell at the stroke of the thunderbolt.
Indra made wide room for his charioteer Kutsa on the same chariot, in the winning of the sun.
Like a hawk, he shook off the head of the Dāsa Namuci while [extracting] for him the exhilarating stalk;
he protected Namī Sāpya as he slept, and filled him with wealth, with food, and with well-being.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, you shattered with your might the firm fortresses of Pipru, who possessed the craft of a serpent.
O bounteous giver, you bestowed that imperishable wealth as a gift upon the worshipper Ṛjiśvan.

Indra, whose favor is most helpful, [slain] Vetasu, who had ten mothers and ten fingers, and the impetuous Tugra; he released him again and again for the sake of light, as one might release a calf to its mother.
He, unopposed, overcomes his rivals, bearing in his hand the Vṛtra-slaying thunderbolt;
standing upon his two bay steeds like a gambler on the gaming board, they carry the lofty Indra, yoked by a word.

May we win through your new protection, O Indra; thus the Pūrus have praised you with sacrifices. When you shattered the seven autumnal fortresses—the Dāsa strongholds that were their refuge—you bestowed them upon Purukutsa, bestowing your favor.
O Indra, you were the ancient increaser; bestowing wealth upon Uśanas Kāvya, you gave away Navavāstva, who was not to be handed over, as his own grandson to his great father.
O Indra, you, the shaker, set in motion the shaking waters, flowing like rivers;
when you, O hero, carried across the ocean, bring Turvaśa and Yadu safely to the further shore.
All that was yours in the battle, O Indra; you laid Dhuni and Cumuri to sleep.
Dabhīti, kindling the fuel and cooking the oblation, shone forth for you with his hymns while pressing the Soma.
O Hero, these invocations of the most frequent singer call upon you, the one to be invoked;
the newest prayers, like wealth and abundant power, go forth with eloquence to you who stand upon the chariot, the ageless one.
I praise that Indra, who is known, who is carried by songs, who is magnified by hymns at the sacrifice;
whose greatness, possessing manifold powers, surpasses both heaven and earth in its vastness.
He, indeed, made the pathless darkness possessed of paths by means of the sun.
O self-powerful one, when do mortals, desiring to worship, not violate your ordinance, O Immortal?
Where indeed is that Indra who performed those deeds? Among what people does he wander, and among which tribes?
What sacrifice is pleasing to your mind and your desire? What is the hymn, O Indra, and who is that Hotar-priest?
For now, O many-invoked one, your ancient friends who were born of old have been active for you; be mindful of those who are middlemost, as well as the most recent, and even of the youngest.
Inquiring about him, the later ones have followed after your ancient deeds of renown, O Indra. We praise you, O hero who are borne by our prayers, as great as we know you to be.
The host of the Rakṣas has risen up against you, who were born mighty; stand firm against that!
With your ancient, allied friend, the thunderbolt, O bold one, drive those away.
But hear now, O Indra, hero who supports the poets, the prayer of this present worshipper;
for you have from of old been the kinsman of our fathers, ever ready to be invoked in our desire.
Bring Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, and the Maruts today for our protection;
bring Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Agni, Purandhi, Savitṛ, the plants, and the mountains.
O you of many powers, O worthy of sacrifice, these singers here honor you with hymns.
Hear the call of those who invoke you; being invoked, there is none other like you among the immortals.
Now come to my song, O wise one, with all the worshipful sons of strength;
those who were fire-tongued guardians of the *ṛta*, who made Manu subordinate to the Dasyu.
Be our leader on easy paths and on difficult ones, you who are the wise maker of ways.
With those steeds of yours that are unwearied, broad, and most excellent at carrying, with them, O Indra, bring us to booty.
Him who alone is the one to be invoked among the peoples—that Indra, I shall celebrate with these songs;
he who rules as a bull, possessed of virile power, the true hero, of many wondrous deeds, and mighty.

Him indeed our ancient fathers, the Navagvas, the seven sages, impelled with their prayers— the one who reaches the giver, the overcomer, who stands upon the mountains, whose speech is guileless, and who is most powerful.

We implore that Indra for this wealth which possesses many heroes, men, and much food—wealth that is unfailing, undecaying, and heavenly. O Lord of the Bay Steeds, bring that hither so that we may rejoice!
Tell us this, O Indra: have your singers of old indeed obtained your favor?
What is your portion, what is your food, O fierce one, you who strike down the oppressor, you who are invoked by many and possess much wealth, O slayer of the Asuras?

Seeking him, the thunderbolt-wielder standing in his chariot— Indra, for whose song there is now trembling and eloquence— she approaches that mighty one, the powerful grasper, the doer of great deeds, the giver of strength, seeking a path toward him for nourishment.

O self-strong one, with this very magic power and with the mountain swift as thought, you shattered even the unshakable, the firmly fixed, and the solid strongholds with your own might, O exuberant hero, through your boldness.
Him, your most powerful one, the ancient, we would honor with a new prayer as of old;
may that Indra, the measureless and excellent driver, carry us across all difficult passages.
For the person who acts with malice, you have set ablaze the earthly, celestial, and intermediate regions.
O Bull, burn them from every side with your flame; for the hater of sacred prayer, consume both the earth and the waters.
You are the king of the heavenly folk and of the earthly world, O you of brilliant aspect.
Take the thunderbolt in your right hand, O Indra; ageless one, you destroy all magical illusions.
O Indra, bestow upon us well-restrained, great, and unfailing prosperity for the overcoming of enemies—
that prosperity by which you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, make the Dāsa and Ārya Vṛtras, and the Nahuṣa foes, easy to overcome.
O much-invoked one, wise disposer, worthy of sacrifice, come to us with your teams of horses that bring all boons;
those which neither godless man nor god can restrain—with them come quickly toward me.
O Indra, when the Soma is pressed, you are closely united with it— at the hymn of praise, at the sacred word,
and at the recited chant— whenever, O Maghavan, you go forth with your two harnessed bay horses, bearing the thunderbolt in your arms, O Indra.

Whether you helped the presser of Soma in heaven at the decisive moment of the Vṛtra-slaying for the winning of heroes, O Indra, or whether, being yourself unafraid, you subdued the defiant Dasyus while the skillful one was afraid— O Indra.
May Indra be the drinker of the pressed soma; may the fierce one, with his aids, lead the singer forward.
May he create a wide space for the hero who presses the juice, and grant wealth even to the humble singer who praises him.
He comes to the libations with his two bay steeds; he bears the thunderbolt, drinks the Soma, and bestows cattle.
He is the maker of the hero, the manly one possessed of all heroes; he hears the call of the singer, borne by the hymns of praise.

Whatever he has desired, that we have offered to him—to Indra, who from of old has performed deeds for us. When the Soma is pressed, we praise him with recitations and hymns, so that our prayer may be a source of strength for Indra.

For you have made the sacred hymns your means of strengthening; such as these we offer to you, O Indra, with our prayers. When the Soma is pressed, O drinker of the pressed juice, let us perform with sacrifices the most peaceful and delightful acts of service for your delight.
Take notice of us, O Indra, accepting our sacrificial cake; drink the Soma mixed with milk.
Sit upon this sacred grass of the sacrificer; grant wide space for those who are devoted to you.

Rejoice indeed according to your pleasure, O fierce one; let these sacrifices reach you. Let these our invocations reach you, who are invoked by many; toward us, O Indra, may this prayer of ours go for your aid.

O friends, as you gather together at the libations, fill that liberal Indra with Soma-juices. Will he not surely assist us in our struggle? Indra will not neglect the presser of the juice for his protection.
Thus has Indra been praised while the Soma was pressed among the Bharadvājas; may he dwell among the wealthy patrons.
May Indra be the patron of the singer and the giver of wealth that contains all desirable things.

The bull-like exhilaration, the hymn, and the chants are with Indra; he is the drinker of the pressed soma, the consumer of the dregs, the one to be praised by men with hymns, the bountiful lord, the celestial king of songs whose protection is inexhaustible.
The victorious hero, manly and discerning, who hears the call of the singer and provides wide protection;
the Vasu, the praise of men, the sustainer of the poets, the prize-winner—when lauded at the sacrifice, he bestows strength.
O Hero, like the axle of two wheels, your greatness has surpassed both heaven and earth.
O Indra, invoked by many, your many succors have grown forth like the branches of a tree.
O Lord of Might, you of many powers, your aids are like the paths for driving cattle;
they are like the tethering ropes for calves—O Indra, O Bountiful Giver, they are bound yet unbound.
One deed today, and another tomorrow; Indra makes the unreal appear as real in an instant.
In this matter, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Pūṣan are our friends; there is none who can surpass the will of the Noble One.
From thee, O Indra, as waters flow from the back of a mountain, they have brought [thee] hither with hymns and sacrifices.
Seeking booty, we approach thee with these fair praises, as horses go to the racecourse, O thou who art borne by songs.
Neither autumns nor months, nor days, wear Indra out; they do not diminish him.
Though he is already grown, let his body increase further when it is being celebrated with hymns and recited praises.
He does not bend before the firm, nor before the steadfast, nor before the defiant one incited by the Dasyus when he is praised.
Even the lofty mountains are like plains to Indra; even in the deep, there is a ford for him.
O Atri-foe-slayer, drinker of the pressed juice, bestow upon us with your deep and wide [chariot] swift impulses and strengths.
Stand up erect for our protection, remaining unharmed at the dawning of night when the time for departure has come.
Accompany this man for his protection in the encounter; O Indra, protect him from harm here.
Guard him at home and in the forest from injury. May we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.

O impetuous Indra, whatever aid you have—whether it be the lowest, the highest, or that which is in the middle—with those aids protect us well in the slaying of Vṛtra; and with these strengths, O fierce one, make us great.
O Indra, without harming them, strike down the hostilities of the adversary and the fury of the enemy with these [missiles].
With these, you have cast down all attacking Dāsa tribes in every direction for the sake of the Ārya.
O Indra, those who have joined as attackers—whether they be kinsmen or strangers—turning toward us, do thou strike down their wavering strength; destroy their manly powers and drive them away.
A hero indeed overcomes a hero with his physical forms when they both strive in their radiant bodies;
whether they contend for offspring, cattle, progeny, or for waters, they both cry out amidst the two worlds and the fertile fields.
Neither the hero, nor the swift, nor the bold has ever fought against you, nor has anyone who considers himself a warrior.
O Indra, no one among these is your equal; you surpass all these created beings.
He rules over the manly power of both races when the wise ones call upon him in the assembly;
whether for the great Vṛtra-slaying or for a dwelling rich in heroes, he and [his companion] spread themselves out as they extend their reach.
Now indeed, O Indra, when the peoples stir themselves, be our protector and our defender—
those of us who are the most heroic among men, the noble patrons, O Indra, who have placed us at their forefront.
To thee was granted for thy great Indra-power all that was needed in the slaying of Vṛtra;
to thee, O worshipful Indra, were granted dominion and might by the gods in the overcoming of men.
Thus, O Indra, bring our rivals together in battles; take delight in the hostile, godless hordes.
Singing your praises, may we, the Bharadvājas, find the light of day through your protection, O Indra, even now.
Hear us, O Indra; we invoke you, raining down [boons], for the winning of great booty. When the tribes gather together for the battle of heroes, grant us fierce protection on the decisive day.
The prize-winning steed, the son of a prize-winner, invokes you for the winning of great booty that is to be seized.
O Indra, the fist-fighter beholds you as the lord of the virtuous and the deliverer in battles against the Vṛtras, as he fights for cattle.

You urged on the seer in the contest for the sun; you struck down Śuṣṇa for the sake of the worshipper Kutsa. You struck off the head of the invulnerable one, performing a deed worthy of praise for Atithigva.
You brought forward the lofty chariot for the warrior; you aided the fighting bull Daśadyu.
You slew Tugra together with Vetasu; O Indra, you strengthened Tuji as he sang your praises.

O Indra, you have made that hymn of praise mighty; O Hero, you have shattered hundreds and thousands. You struck down the Dāsa Śambara from the mountain and protected Divodāsa with your wondrous aids.
Rejoicing in the acts of faith and in the Soma juices, O Indra, you sent Cumuri to sleep for Dabhīti.
Bestowing favor upon Piṭhīnas, you by your power slew sixty thousand Raji along with his followers.

May I too, along with the patrons, attain that superior favor and power of yours, O Indra— when, O most powerful one, the heroes praise you, the possessor of true heroes, who provide threefold protection to the Nahuṣas.
O Indra, may we be your dearest friends in this invocation for glory;
may Prātardani, the glory of the ruling power, be the most excellent in the slaying of Vṛtras and in the winning of riches.
What has Indra done in the exhilaration of this [Soma], or what in its drinking, or what in its friendship?
What delights have they found in its presence in the past, and what indeed do the present ones find?
In his exhilaration, in his drinking, and in his friendship, Indra has brought about what is real;
both the ancient delights found in his presence and those that are new have been realized as real.

For we do not indeed know the full extent of your greatness, O Maghavan, nor your status as a liberal giver; no one has ever seen the limit of your power, O Indra, even regarding your most recent bounty.
This very power of yours has become manifest, by which you struck down the offspring of Varaśikha;
for when your thunderbolt was hurled, O Indra, even from its roar the furthest limit was shattered by its force.
Indra slew the offspring of Varaśikha, bestowing aid upon Abhyāvartin Cāyamāna;
when he struck down Vṛcīvanta at Hariyūpīyā, the former half [of his army] perished in fear while the latter fled.
O Indra, much-invoked one, three thousand armored men together, seeking glory on the Yavyāvatī river,
the Vṛcīvants, falling before your arrow, went to their destruction like broken vessels.
He whose two ruddy bulls, seeking good pasture, move about between the two worlds, licking their lips— He,
bestowing Turvaśa upon Sṛñjaya, gave Vṛcīvat to Daivavāta, providing for him.
O Agni, the sovereign Maghavan has given me twenty chariot-borne horses with their mates;
this Abhyāvartin, the son of Āyama, bestows them, for this sacrificial fee of the Pārthavas is difficult to attain.
The cows have come; they have brought auspiciousness. Let them sit in the cow-pen and rejoice with us.
May they be here, prolific and many-formed, yielding their milk for Indra through many dawns.
Indra bestows gifts upon the one who sacrifices and the one who gives; he grants more and does not take away what is his own.
Increasing his wealth ever further, he places the god-fearing man upon an unbroken field.
They are not lost, nor does a thief harm them; no enemy or distress dares to attack them.
With those [cows] by which one worships the gods and gives gifts, the owner of the cattle dwells together with them for a long time.
The dust-raising horse does not overtake them; they do not go toward the prepared place of sacrifice.
Far-striding and fearless, those cows of the mortal sacrificer roam along after them.
The cows are Bhaga; the cows Indra has looked upon for me; the cows are the first draught of Soma.
O people, these which are the cows belong to Indra; with my heart and even with my mind, I desire Indra.
O cows, you make even the emaciated fat; you make even the unlovely beautiful of countenance.
You make the home auspicious, O you of auspicious speech; your great vitality is proclaimed in the assemblies.
May you be rich in offspring, grazing on good pasture, drinking pure waters at a fine watering-place;
let not the thief nor the malicious man master you, and may the missile of Rudra avoid you.
Let this mixing be added; let it be mixed into these cows, into the semen of the bull, and into your own virility, O Indra.
The men have sought Indra for friendship, seeking to attain his great favor and desiring his goodwill;
for he, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is a great giver. Worship him, the great and joyous one, for protection.
In whose hand men have placed their strength, who stands upon the golden chariot as its lord;
in whose two firm hands the reins are held, and who has yoked the vigorous stallions on the path.
For the sake of glory, your feet have been anointed with homage; bold wielder of the thunderbolt, you are rich in strength and gifts.
Clothed in a fragrant mantle, fair to behold, you have become as vigorous as the sun in your dancing.
That Soma has become most thoroughly mixed when it is pressed— the one in which the cooked offering is prepared and roasted grains are present—
while the men, praising Indra, performing sacred prayers, and reciting hymns, are most beloved by the gods.
No limit has been set to the extent of this thy power; indeed, by thy greatness thou hast pushed apart the two worlds, heaven and earth.
The patron, hastening with his aid, fills them both, as one who gathers herds together in the waters.
Thus indeed is Indra, the far-reaching one, easy to invoke; he is the hero with golden jaws, who comes with or without a call.
For even as soon as he was born, he possessed unequalled strength; he slays many Vṛtras and strikes down the Dasyus.
He has grown even greater for heroic power; he alone, undecaying, bestows riches.
Indra has surpassed heaven and earth; indeed, both worlds are but half of him.

Now I consider his divine power to be vast; no one can diminish those things which he has established. Day after day the sun has become visible; the one of noble intellect has widely laid out the dwellings.
Even now, and even at this moment, is that work of the rivers, when you, O Indra, carved out a path for them.
The mountains settled down like those sitting at a feast; by you, O doer of good deeds, the realms were made firm.
This is indeed true: there is no other like you, O Indra—neither god nor mortal is greater.
You slew the serpent who lay encompassing the flood; you released the waters toward the ocean.
O Indra, you split apart the waters and the gates in all directions; you shattered the firmness of the mountain.
You became the king of the moving world and of the peoples, generating at once the sun, the sky, and the dawn.
You alone have become the lord of riches, O Indra; you have placed the peoples within your hands.
Among their offspring, their waters, their progeny, and the sun, the people have raised various voices in invocation.
Out of fear of you, O Indra, all the earthly realms—even those that are unshakable—are shaken;
heaven and earth, the mountains, and the forests—all that is firm fears at your onset.
O Indra, with Kutsa you fought against the voracious Śuṣṇa and Kuyava in the quest for cattle;
then, at the onset of the day, you stole the wheel of the sun and cast away his evils.

You struck down the hundreds of the Dasyu Śambara’s impregnable fortresses, O Lord of Power, when you, by your might, bestowed riches upon Divodāsa who pressed the soma and poured the libation, and upon the praising Bharadvāja.
O you of true strength, mount your terrible chariot for the great battle, O you of many manly deeds!
Come hither on your long journey with your aid toward me; and being renowned, make yourself heard among all people.
I have fashioned with my lips most excellent and unprecedented words for this great hero, the powerful and swift one— for the exuberant wielder of the thunderbolt, for the steadfast one.
He, being praised by the wise, caused his two parents to dwell with the Sun; shattering the mountain while being lauded by the well-intentioned singers, he released the confinement of the ruddy cows.
With his carriers, the singers who kneel in devotion, he—performing many deeds—has repeatedly won the cattle;
as a friend among friends and a seer among seers, he, the destroyer of forts, shattered the strongholds with his companions.
O Bull of the peoples, lover of songs, come forth toward the singer with girdles [of light], with great spoils, and with mighty strengths, accompanied by many heroes, for our well-being.
Urged on by his own impetuous might, Indra, the subduer of the swift, drove the waters to the right.
Thus released, they flowed forth unrestrained; day after day they performed their unerring task for the sake of heaven.
O Indra, O bull, grant us that most powerful exhilaration which is victorious and bountiful;
may it win for us the possession of fine horses, and may it, with its own steeds, overcome Vritras and enemies in battles.
For the people with contending voices call upon you, O Indra, for protection in the battle for heroes;
you, with the inspired singers, have overcome the Paṇis, and the steed aided by you wins the prize.
O Indra, O Hero, you have slain both kinds of enemies—the Dāsas and the Āryas—like trees with well-honed weapons; O most manly of men, you rend them in battle.
As such, O Indra, be our friend with your unailing aids, the protector of all life, increasing us for our prosperity.
When we call upon you in the winning of the light, O Hero, as we fight in battles over the division of spoils.

Surely, O Indra, may you be ours for the future as well; be gracious to us and present for our aid. Thus praising, under the protection of the Mighty One, may we be the best winners of cattle on the decisive day.
Many songs have gathered unto you, O Indra, and from you proceed abundant thoughts. Both ancient and recent praises of the seers, as well as hymns and chants, have vied for your favor.
He who is invoked by many, praised by many, the skillful one, alone glorified by sacrifices;
like a chariot harnessed for great power, may Indra be celebrated by us with hymns of praise.
Him whom neither prayers nor songs harm, Indra they reach and cause to grow;
when a hundred or a thousand singers praise him who delights in song, all that is for his well-being.
For him, as for the sky with the moon, the months have mingled; the Soma has been offered into Indra.
As waters flow together toward people in the desert, so have the invocations increased by means of sacrifices.

To him has this great hymn of praise been spoken, to this Indra has the song of praise been uttered with inspired thoughts, so that in the great battle against Vṛtra, Indra may be the protector of all life and the increaser of our strength.
When will our prayers find their rest in your chariot? When will you grant the singer nourishment for a thousandfold prosperity?
When will you clothe this hymn with wealth? And when will you make our thoughts rich in the prize of booty?
When indeed will that happen, O Indra, when you shall settle men with men, heroes with heroes, and cause the non-conquerors to flee?
May you win the threefold cattle in the contests for kine; O Indra, bestow upon us splendor that shines like the sun.

O Indra, most powerful one, when indeed will you make that all-sustaining sacred word (*brahman*) for the singer? When will you yoke your teams like our prayers? When will you come to the invocations accompanied by gifts of cattle?

Bestow upon the singer gifts of cattle, horses resplendent with wealth, and nourishments renowned for their vigor; O Indra, swell the milch-cow that is easy to milk, and let her shine forth with brilliant luster among the Bharadvājas.
Lead us now to that stronghold in a different way, O Hero, since you, O Śakra, are praised for opening the doors.
Let us not be excluded from the cow that milks the bright [soma]; O Sage, quicken the Aṅgirases with our prayer.

Truly, thy exhilarations are for all people; truly, so are the riches that belong to the earth. Truly, thou hast been the distributor of spoils of war, since thou didst maintain divine power among the gods.
I have sacrificed following his people's strength; they have fully established themselves for heroic valor.
For the spear-grasper and the impetuous steed, they direct their will even toward the slaying of Vṛtra.
United aids, manly powers, and heroic strengths accompany Indra;
like rivers rushing to the ocean, our songs—impetuous with hymns—enter him who is wide-extending.
Being praised, O Indra, release for us a spring of wealth, of that treasure which is most radiant;
you have become the peerless lord of men, the sole king of the entire world.
Hear that which is worthy of being heard, O you who are devoted to worship; like the sky [overshadows] the earth, so [do you cover us] with the riches of the noble one.
May you be pleased toward us with your power, manifesting through your vital strength age after age.
Hither, O fierce Indra, let your yoked bay horses bring your chariot that contains all treasures;
for even the poor man, possessing the light of heaven, calls upon you—may we today prosper as your companions at the feast.
To the wooden vat the tawny drops have gone; being purified, they have become straight-flowing.
May Indra, our ancient one, drink of this; may the heavenly King drink of the exhilarating Soma juice.
Racing toward the powerful Indra on well-wheeled chariots, let the horses bear him toward glory, striving straight for it; never indeed shall the immortality of Vāyu fail.
Indra, the most excellent and most active among the wealthy, sends forth his bounty— the gift by which,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, you deliver us from distress and, O bold one, distribute riches among the patrons.
Indra is the giver of enduring strength; may Indra, whose greatness has increased, be magnified by our songs.
May Indra be the most effective slayer of Vṛtra, that hero; as such, the patron, hastening forward, bestows gifts upon us.

From here he has come; may the most wonderful Indra bear up our great and glorious invocation. On the path of the divine host, the Bountiful One wins the most praiseworthy prayer and the gift of the people.
Even from afar, his ears are near; speaking aloud, he makes the sound of Indra's voice resound.
May this invocation of the gods come to him; may this recited hymn turn Indra toward me.
With the highest devotion, I have celebrated with hymns that ancient and undecaying Indra whom you [seek].
Both sacred prayers and songs have been offered together unto him; may the great hymn of praise increase further within Indra.
May the sacrifice and Soma strengthen Indra; may the sacred formulation, the songs, the hymns, and the prayers strengthen him.
May the dawns at their rising strengthen him; may the nights, the months, the autumns, and the days strengthen Indra.

Thus have we brought hither for our protection the one born for complete power, who has grown great for renowned bounty—the mighty and fierce one, O sage; let us now invite him for aid in the battles against Vṛtra.
Of the sweet, divine, and inspired Vahni, the sage-like mind of the speech of honey—
of that [speech] which accompanies us among the gods, O Lord, do thou bestow upon the singer [wealth] headed by cattle.
Desiring the kine, he has gone around the mountain with those whose thoughts are fixed on the Law, yoking his team at the time of the Law;
Indra shattered the unbroken ridge of Vala and fought down the Paṇis with his words.
This drop, O Indra, has illuminated the nights that were unlit, through the autumns, at evening and at dawn.
They have established him as the banner of days from of old; he has brought forth the Dawns of pure birth.
Shining with his own light, he has caused the unshining to glow; by the Eternal Law, he has illumined many ancient things.
He has moved along with horses yoked by the Eternal Law, reaching the people with a sun-finding navel.
Now, O ancient King, being praised, swell forth abundant nourishments for the singer so that he may bestow wealth;
grant waters, medicinal herbs, forests free from poison, cattle, horses, and men to him who praises you.
O Indra, drink; the juice is pressed for your exhilaration. Unharness your two bay steeds, your companions.
And sing forth, having seated yourself in our assembly; then bestow vigor upon the singer for the sacrifice.
Drink of this, O Indra, of which you drank at your birth for exhilaration and for wisdom, O mighty one.
For you, the men, the cows, the waters, and the pressing-stone have together prepared this Soma-drop for your drinking.
The fire is kindled, O Indra, and the Soma is pressed; let your bay horses, the swiftest bearers, carry you hither.
With a mind directed toward you, I call upon you repeatedly; O Indra, come for our great prosperity.
Come hither; you have always come with longing, O Indra, with a great mind to the drinking of Soma.
Listen to these our prayers, and then let the sacrifice bestow vigor upon your body.

O Indra, whether you are in the distant sky, or elsewhere, or in your own abode, wherever you may be—come from there with your team of horses for our protection; O lover of songs, being of one mind with the Maruts, protect our sacrifice.
Come to the sacrifice without anger; for you the pressed drops flow clear.
Like cows to their own stall, O wielder of the thunderbolt, come to us, O Indra, first among those worthy of worship.
With that well-fashioned, most excellent cup of yours, with which you constantly drink the wave of honeyed Soma—drink from it!
The Adhvaryu has stepped forward for you; let your thunderbolt, O Indra, turn toward the cattle.
This drop, the bull of every form, the Soma, has been prepared for the bull Indra.
Drink it, O Lord of Bay Horses, steadfast driver, O fierce one, over which you have presided from of old and which is your food.
O Indra, the pressed Soma is better than the unpressed; this is more excellent for the joy of one who knows. Come to this sacrifice, O Conqueror, and with it fill yourself with all powers.
We call upon you, O Indra; come hither. Let the Soma be sufficient for your body.
O Śatakratu, rejoice in the pressed juices; protect us in battles and among our people.
Bring all [offerings] to him who desires to drink, the one who knows all,
the one who comes readily, the one who goes forth, the hero who does not lag behind.
Come toward him with Soma juices, [you who are] the greatest drinker of Soma;
with vessels, [come] to the impetuous Indra with the pressed drops.
If you adorn yourselves with the pressed drops, with the Soma juices—the wise one knows all; boldly he seeks each and every one of them.
O Adhvaryu, bring forth this pressed juice for him, for him alone! Will he not protect us from the curse of every arrogant kinsman?
In whose exhilaration you delivered that Śambara over to Divodāsa—this is that Soma pressed for you, O Indra; drink!
O Indra, that sharp-pressed exhilarating drink whose beginning, middle, and end you guard—this is that Soma pressed for you; drink it!
In whose exhilaration you released the cows that were held fast within the rock—this is that Soma pressed for you, O Indra; drink!
O Indra, you who, exhilarated by this draught, have taken up the power of Maghavan—this is that Soma pressed for you; drink!
O Indra, Lord of the Self-Sustaining Power, that pressed Soma which is the wealthiest among the wealthy and the most radiant among the radiant— that is your intoxication.
O you who are powerful, most mighty in power, the giver of wealth and of hymns—that pressed Soma is yours, O Indra; it is your exhilarating draught, O Lord of Self-Existence.

That pressed Soma which, O Indra, Lord of the Self-Sustaining Power (*svadhā*), is your intoxicant— by which you are not surpassed in might by the aged, nor by the swift with their own aids— [that is yours].
I praise that Indra of yours, the lord of power, who is never struck down— the hero who conquers all, most bountiful, and the protector of all people.
The songs which magnify him, the lord of swift bounty—
verily, both the divine worlds, heaven and earth, honor his vital strength.
That greatness of yours, for Indra, I spread out as a seat for this hymn— [the greatness] whose aids, like inspired songs,
grow forth together from a common dwelling.
Mitra, the most recent one, has found skill; having drunk, he has perceived what is better for the gods.
Having won with the *staulā* and *dhautarī* dice, he has become a wide protector for his friends.
On the path of Truth, the Ordainer has drunk; for the sake of glory, the gods have set their minds [upon him].
Assuming his great name through his words, the beloved one, beautiful to behold, has revealed his form.
Bestow upon us most resplendent skill; ward off the many hostilities of men.
By your powers, grant us more abundant vigor, and aid us in the winning of wealth.
O Indra, O Maghavan, we have become yours; O Lord of the Bay Steeds, do not turn away from us as a giver.
No kinsman whatsoever is seen among mortals; why then do they call you the one who urges on the weak?
O Bull, do not abandon us to the one who is stingy; O Wealthy One, may we suffer no harm in your friendship.
O Indra, you have many adversaries among the people; slay those who do not press the Soma, root out those who do not give!
Like thundering clouds, Indra sends forth gifts of horses and cattle;
from of old you have been the sustainer of the singer. Let not the stingy ones deceive you, O Maghavan.
O hero, Adhvaryu, bring the pressed juices for the great Indra; for he is the king of this [soma], he who has grown strong through the ancient and the new songs of the praising seers.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], Indra, the knower of many forms, struck down the Vṛtras who were irresistible.
Offer up for him that Soma rich in sweetness, so that he, the hero with the beautiful jaws, may drink it.
May Indra be the drinker of the pressed soma, slaying Vṛtra with his thunderbolt while exhilarated;
may he come even from afar to the sacrifice, the Vasu who protects our prayers and sustains the poets.
This is that very vessel for Indra’s drinking; Indra’s beloved nectar has been drunk. May it exhilarate the god for his goodwill; may it drive away hatred from us and drive away distress.

O Hero, exhilarated by these [soma-draughts], slay the enemies—the kinsmen and the strangers, O Maghavan, the unfriendly foes. Against those who advance with their armies and point [us out as targets], O Indra, crush them and strike them down, driving them away.
O Maghavan Indra, in these battles of ours, grant us great freedom and an easy path;
for the winning of waters, of progeny, and of descendants, O Indra, place our patrons on your side.
May the bay steeds, the virile ones, being harnessed—horses with virile chariots and virile reins—come toward us;
may they, the well-yoked virile carriers of the thunderbolt, bring you here for the sake of the virile exhilaration.
O Bull, thy vigorous [drops] have entered the vat, dripping with clarity like waves rejoicing;
O Indra, for thee, the bull, they bring the pressed soma with its vigorous juices, for thee, the vigorous one.
You are the bull of heaven, the bull of earth; you are the bull of the rivers, O bull, of the standing waters.
For you, the bull, the drop has swelled—its sweet juice, the honeyed draught, for your choice.
This god, being born with power, with Indra as his ally, struck down Paṇi;
this Indu stole away the weapons of his own father and the magic arts of the malevolent one.
He made the dawns have a good husband; he placed light within the sun. He found the threefold hidden nectar in the three luminous realms of heaven.
He propped apart heaven and earth; he yoked the chariot with its seven reins.
By his power, he placed the cooked milk within the cows; Soma held fast the fountain with its ten mechanisms.
He who, by his skillful guidance, brought Turvaśa and Yadu from afar—
Indra is our youthful friend.
Bestowing vigor even upon one who is no sage, and with even a horse that is not swift,
Indra is the winner of the staked prize.
Great are his guidances, and many are his praises;
his aids do not fail.
O friends, sing praises and chant aloud for him who is drawn by our sacred prayer;
for he is our great protector.
O slayer of Vṛtra, you are the protector of one, you are the protector of two,
and also of such as we are.
You lead us past our enemies; you make us reciters of hymns. O hero among men, you are called "possessor of good heroes."
With hymns, I call upon the Brahman, the bearer of the sacred word, the friend worthy of praise, as one calls a cow for milking.
In whose two hands they say all treasures are deposited from of old—
of that hero who overcomes hostile armies.
O wielder of the stone, O Lord of Might, you who are unbending, tear asunder even the firm fortresses of men; destroy their magical illusions.
O true one, O Soma-drinker, O Indra, Lord of spoils,
we who desire glory have invoked you.
