Whether you were such as you were aforetime, or whether you are now such when the prize is set,
you who are to be invoked— listen to our call!
With our prayers and with swift steeds, O Indra, may we win through you the prize-winning horses and the wealth set before us that brings renown.
O Hero, lover of songs, you have indeed become great, O Indra, when the prize is set; you are to be sought out in the fray for booty.
O slayer of enemies, that aid of yours which is most swift in its onset— with that, impel our chariot forward.
O most skilled charioteer, with our attacking chariot, may you,
the victorious one, win the wealth that has been set before us.
Praise him who is alone, the one who observes all people;
he was born as the Lord, the one of manly will.
O Indra, you who have been a kinsman to those who sing your praises, a gracious friend with your aid— such as you are, O Indra, be merciful to us!
Take up the thunderbolt in your hands for the slaying of the Rākṣasas, O wielder of the thunderbolt; may you utterly overcome our rivals.
I invoke the ancient companion of riches, the ally who impels the singer, the one most frequently borne by sacred prayers.
For he alone rules over all earthly treasures; he is the most beloved of singers, the irresistible one.
O Lord of Cattle, boldly fulfill our desire with your teams of horses, with riches consisting of horses and cattle.
Sing that song for you at the libation for the one invoked by many, the warrior,
which brings welfare like [a blessing] to a powerful bull.
The Vasu does not indeed withhold the gift of wealth consisting of cattle,
once he has heard our songs.
May the slayer of Dasyus indeed go to this man’s cow-filled stall;
with his powers, may he open it for us.
O Śatakratu, these songs have cried out toward you,
O Indra, as mother cows low toward their calf.
Your friendship is difficult to attain; you are a bull for one who desires cattle, O hero;
be a horse for one who desires horses.
Rejoice indeed in the soma-juice for the sake of great bounty through your own body;
do not deliver your worshipper to reproach.
O lover of songs, these hymns reach out to you at every pressing,
like milch-cows lowing toward their calf.
To him who is most frequent among many, in the contest of the praisers,
for those striving to win the prize with prizes.
O Indra, may our hymn of praise be most effective and closest to you;
impel us toward great wealth.
Bṛbu has taken his stand upon the highest head of the Paṇis,
like the broad forest-thicket on the banks of the Gaṅgā.
He whose auspicious gift, flowing like the wind, is thousandfold,
bestows it immediately for giving.
Therefore, all the noble singers always praise us well— Bṛbu, the most liberal giver of thousands, the patron who bestows thousands most abundantly.
For we poets indeed invoke you for the winning of booty;
O Indra, lord of the virtuous, men invoke you against the Vṛtras, and you [invoke] the horse in the races.
As such, O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, being boldly praised by us, O lord of the stone-weaponed mace—
O Indra, bestow upon us cattle, horses, and chariots, and grant us ever-present strength, as if for a victor.
Him who is the all-conquering, far-seeing one, that Indra we invoke;
O Lord of the good, with a thousand testicles and great manly vigor, be our strengthener in battles.

You press down upon the people with fury like a bull, O impetuous one, bounteous giver, worthy of praise. Be our protector in the great contest for wealth, for our bodies, for the waters, and for the sun.
O Indra, bring us the highest, most powerful, and fulfilling glory,
O fair-cheeked one, by which you, O wondrous wielder of the thunderbolt, have filled both these worlds, heaven and earth.
We invoke you, O King, the fierce one who subdues the peoples, among the gods for our protection.
O Vasu, make all our wavering things firm; make our enemies easy to overcome.
O Indra, whatever vigor and manly strength exists among the Nahuṣa tribes,
or whatever splendor belongs to the five peoples— bring all those heroic powers hither at once.
Or whatever virile power you have among the Tṛkṣus, O Maghavan, or among the Druhyus, or among the people of Pūru—
bestow all that upon us, so that we may prevail over our enemies in the contest for men and conquer them in battles.
O Indra, grant a threefold protection, a triple refuge, and a secure shelter to the generous patrons and to me; ward off the missile from them.
Those who, with minds intent on cattle, have overcome the enemy and strike him down with boldness—
O Indra, Maghavan, lover of songs, be our closest protector of our bodies.
And so, O Indra, be for our prosperity;
do not abandon us in battle when the feathered arrows with sharpened points fly through the mid-air.
Where heroes stretch out their bodies and find the dear protection of the fathers—there, grant shelter for our own bodies and for our offspring; ward off the unseen hostilities.
O Indra, when you urge the horses forth in the great contest for wealth,
on the uneven road and the crooked path, like falcons seeking glory;
Like rivers rushing down a slope, they speed along when they follow the sound of the whip;
like birds circling for meat, they are held fast by the arms within the cow.
Truly, this [Soma] is sweet and indeed honeyed; truly, it is strong and indeed flavorful. And now, no one at all can withstand Indra in battles when he has drunk of it.
This sweet juice here has been most intoxicating, in which Indra delighted during the slaying of Vṛtra—
he who struck down the many great exploits of Śambara and his ninety-nine fortresses.
This [Soma], when drunk by me, raises up my voice; this has awakened the yearning wisdom.
This wise one has measured out the six wide expanses, beyond which no world exists at all.
He is he who made the breadth of the earth and the height of heaven; he is that very one. This Soma has established the nectar in the three flowing rivers and the broad mid-air.
He has found the wondrously-beheld flood at the forefront of the dawns that dwell in the light.
This Great One, the Bull accompanied by the Maruts, has propped up the sky with a mighty pillar.
Drink boldly the Soma from the jar, O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer, hero among the treasures in battle!
At the midday libation, pour it down; as the abode of wealth, bestow wealth upon us.
O Indra, look out for us like a leader; lead us further toward greater prosperity.
Be a good ferryman who carries us across; be a wise guide and a benevolent leader.
O Knower, lead us to a wide world, to the light of heaven that is free from fear and brings well-being.
O Indra, lofty and steadfast are your arms; may we take refuge beneath them, your great protection.
O Indra, place us upon the broadest chariot-seat, drawn by your two most swift horses, O Lord of a hundred powers!
Bring us the most excellent nourishment among all foods; O Maghavan, let not the wealth of the enemy overcome us.
O Indra, be gracious; desire life for me. Sharpen my inspired thought like the edge of iron.
Whatever I, devoted to you, speak here, accept that; make me one who possesses the gods.
Indra the protector, Indra the helper, the hero Indra who is easily invoked at every call—I invoke Śakra, Indra who is invoked by many. May the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us.
May Indra, the good protector, the possessor of wealth, with his aids, be gracious to us—he who possesses all knowledge.
May he drive away our enemies and grant us safety; may we be masters of heroic strength.
May we abide in the good-will of that one worthy of sacrifice, and in his auspicious favor. May that Indra, the excellent protector and possessor of wealth, drive our enemies far away from us.
Toward you, O Indra, our songs, prayers, and teams of horses rush like waves down a slope.
Like a wide expanse, you gather for yourself many libations, wealth, waters, and cows, O wielder of the thunderbolt, along with the drops of Soma.
Who shall praise him? Who shall satisfy him? Who shall sacrifice to him, since the bounteous one ever protects the fierce one?
Striking them down like two feet, he makes one after another—first and then last—by his mighty powers.
The hero is heard of as subduing every fierce man, leading one after another beyond [conflict];
Indra, the king of both worlds, whose hostilities increase, thrice stirs the people of men.
He casts aside his friendships with the former ones; speeding onward, he goes with others.
Shaking off those who have not experienced him, Indra triumphs through many autumns.

He has become the counterpart of every form; that is his form for the purpose of being seen. Indra moves in many forms through his powers of illusion (*māyā*), for ten hundred bay steeds are harnessed to him.
Yoking his two bay horses to the chariot, Tvaṣṭṛ rules here with great power.
Who among those who sit as patrons would ever take the side of the enemy? And who, while the patrons remain seated, would favor the foe?
O gods, we have come to a land where there are no pastures; though the earth is vast, it has become a place of distress.
O Bṛhaspati, provide guidance in the search for cattle; O Indra, show the path to this singer who stands thus.
Day after day, she drove away the similar black offspring from their dwelling to the other side;
the bull struck down the two Dāsas, Varcin and Śambara, who were haggling over wealth at the enclosure of the waters.
Prastoka has now given you, O Indra, ten coffers of wealth and ten prize-winning horses. From Divodāsa we have received the gift of Atithigva; we have taken possession of the Śambara treasure.
Ten horses, ten chests, ten garments and provisions,
and ten lumps of gold— these I have won from Divodāsa.
Aśvatha gave ten chariots with side-horses and a hundred cows to the Atharvans and to Pāyu.
Sārñjaya has offered worship to the Bharadvājas, who bestow great wealth beneficial to all people.
O Lord of the Forest, may you be firm of limb, our friend, a furtherer, and a hero of great strength;
bound with cow-hides, be steadfast, and let your rider conquer all that is to be won.
Its power was drawn forth from heaven and earth; its force was brought together from the trees.
Worship with an oblation the chariot of Indra—the thunderbolt of Indra, the vigor of the waters, encompassed by cattle.
The thunderbolt of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, and the navel of Varuṇa— O divine chariot, enjoying this our offering of oblations, accept these gifts.
Make the earth and the sky resound; let the world scattered in many places take heed of you. O drum, in alliance with Indra and the gods, drive our enemies far, even to the furthest distance.
Thunder forth strength; bestow vigor upon us; roar aloud, driving away misfortunes.
O drum, blow away all ill-fortune from here; you are Indra’s fist—be firm!
Drive those away and bring these back; the drum speaks loudly as a signal. Our heroes, winged with horses, advance together; O Indra, let our chariot-warriors be victorious!
Sacrifice after sacrifice, with song after song, we shall offer praise for your sake to Agni, for his skill;
we shall extol the immortal Jātavedas as a beloved friend.
Let us, being well-disposed toward him, worship the Son of Strength with offerings for the gift of oblations;
may he be our helper in battles, may he be our increaser, and may he be the protector of our bodies.
For you, O Agni, are a bull, ageless and great; you shine with your flame. O pure one, blazing with undecaying radiance, shine forth brilliantly with your beautiful splendors!

O Agni, you sacrifice to the great gods; you shall sacrifice to them in due order through your wisdom and your wondrous power. Turn them hither for our protection; grant us strength and win it for us.
Him whom the waters, the stones, and the woods nourish as the embryo of Cosmic Order—
he who is produced by men with force upon the summit of the earth.
He who has filled both worlds with his radiance hastens through the sky with smoke;
he has become visible through the darkness in the nights—reddish-brown among the dark ones, the ruddy bull among the dark ones.
O Agni, with your great beams of light and with your bright radiance, O God, being kindled by Bharadvāja, O youngest one, shine upon us with wealth, O bright one; shine with splendor, O purifier!
O Agni, you are the lord of house of all human clans;
O youngest one, protect your kindler from distress with a hundred fortresses for a hundred winters, as well as those who give to your praisers.
O Wondrous One, O Vasu, impel bounties toward us with your aid.
You, O Agni, are the charioteer of this wealth; find a firm footing for our offspring.
Protect our children and descendants with your unfailing and tireless guardians; O Agni, ward off from us the divine wrath and the deceptions of the godless.
O friends, drive hither with a newest song the cow who yields nectar;
release her who does not shrink away.
She who has milked immortal fame for the self-luminous host of Maruts;
she who is in the favor of the swift Maruts, she who comes hither with their blessings.
For Bharadvāja,
you have twice milked forth the cow who yields all things, and the nourishment that provides sustenance for all.
I praise him for my purpose— him who is like Indra in his skillful wisdom, like Varuṇa in his power of illusion, like Aryaman in his joy, and like Viṣṇu in his wide-reaching bounty.
Like the brilliant host of Maruts, loud-sounding and invincible, may he bring together hundreds and thousands from among the people;
may he make hidden treasures manifest, and may he make wealth easy for us to find.
O Pūṣan, hasten toward me; I would now whisper into your ear, O glowing one:
"The hostile enmities of the enemy are evil."
Do not uproot the Kākambīra tree, for you shall utterly destroy the revilers; nor indeed, even for a single day, shall the Sun hold the necks of the bird.
May your friendship be like that of a leather bag— free from wild beasts,
without a leak, well-filled, and overflowing with curds.
For you are beyond mortals and equal to the gods in glory;
O Pūṣan, look upon us in battles and protect us now as you did of old.
O shakers, may the guidance of the benevolent one be for us—
his bounty, whether he be a god or a mortal who strives to sacrifice, O Maruts, you who are swift in worship.
The praise of whom, even as soon as it is uttered, the god Sūrya goes around the sky;
the Maruts have assumed brilliant power and a name worthy of sacrifice—their power is Vṛtra-slaying, their power is supreme, their power is Vṛtra-slaying.
Once indeed heaven was born; once the earth was born. Once was the milk of Pṛśni milked; no other is born after that.
I praise the people of holy vows with newest songs—Mitra and Varuṇa, who grant favor.
May they come hither; may they listen here—the noble rulers Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni.
To be praised by every people at the sacrifices, the one of undeluded will, the steward of the two young maidens,
the child of heaven, the son of strength, Agni, the ruddy banner of the sacrifice— to him I shall offer worship.

The two daughters of the ruddy one are of different forms: one is adorned with stars, the other belongs to the sun. Moving apart from each other, the two purifiers traverse the space; being praised in song, they reach the famous hymn.
Toward Vāyu, with a lofty hymn, do I seek—the one of vast wealth, possessor of all boons, and filler of the chariot.
O you who are worthy of sacrifice, as a sage you desire to honor the sage, you who possess teams of horses that travel with brilliant paths.

May that radiant chariot of the Aśvins, which yokes itself by thought, conceal my form for me— that chariot wherewith, O Nāsatyas, you come as heroes to hasten toward our dwelling, for the sake of our offspring and ourselves.
O Parjanya and Vāta, bulls of the earth, quicken the watery soil.
O sages who hear the truth, by whose songs you sustain the world, bring the world to life.

The daughter of the thunderbolt, the many-colored Sarasvatī, the wife of heroes, bestows inspired thought. In harmony with the divine dames, may she grant the singer an unassailable refuge and a flawless shelter.

With eloquence, he has reached the sun, impelled by desire, [seeking] the protector of every path. May that Pūṣan grant us riches with gold at their head; may he bring each and every prayer to fulfillment.

May the radiant Hotṛ Agni worship Tvaṣṭṛ— the one who receives the first portion, the glorious, the bestower of vigor, the god with beautiful hands and lovely arms, the skillful, the one easily invoked, and the lord of the dwellings.
With these songs, we shall magnify Rudra, the father of the world, by day and by night;
impelled by the sage, let us separately invoke him—the vast, lofty, undecaying, and most gracious one.
O youthful, wise, and worshipful Maruts, come to the beloved dwelling of the singer;
for you, increasing in strength, quicken even the dull, O heroes, as you approach like the Aṅgirases.
Forward to the hero, the powerful and swift one, like a herdsman driving his cattle home;
he shall touch the heights of the sky with the hymns of the famous singer, as if with the rays of light upon his body.
Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms three times for the sake of man when he was oppressed—
may we rejoice in wealth, in our own bodies, and in our offspring, while abiding under the protection you provide.
May Ahi Budhnya with the waters and hymns, may Parvata, and may Savitṛ grant us this favor; may the plants, the liberal Rātiṣāc, Bhaga, and Purandhi quicken us toward wealth.
Now grant us wealth that moves on chariots, filling the people, rich in heroes, a great guardian of Truth—
a dwelling place that does not age, by which we may overcome the godless rival tribes and prevail over the god-fearing peoples.
With prostrations, I invoke for mercy the goddess Aditi, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni;
Aryaman who bestows gifts, the gracious one, the gods who are protectors, Savitṛ, and Bhaga.
O Sūrya, you of great splendor, seek out the gods who possess excellent light and whose fathers are Dakṣa—for the sake of sinlessness—O most mighty one:
those twice-born ones who are observers of the *ṛta*, the truthful, who dwell in heaven, the holy ones whose tongue is Agni.
And may Heaven and Earth, the two vast and blissful worlds, grant us wide dominion and great refuge.
O two Goddesses of Wisdom (Dhiṣaṇās), provide for us a secure dwelling free from danger, so that we may have ample space for our habitation.
May the sons of Rudra, the invincible Vasus, being invoked today, be favorable to us—
those Maruts, the gods, whom we have called upon when placed in either small or great distress.

To whomsoever the two goddesses, Heaven and Earth, have come together, Pūṣan, who bestows ample sacrifice, attends them. O Maruts, when you hear our call and set forth, all beings tremble on your distinguished path.
Sing with a new prayer, O singer, to that hero Indra, the lover of songs;
may he, being praised, hear our call and, being lauded, grant us great spoils of war.

O Waters, you who belong to mankind, grant us uninjured protection; bestow well-being and health upon our children and descendants, for you are the most motherly physicians, the progenitors of all that is stationary and all that moves.
May the divine Savitṛ, the protector, the golden-handed, the worshipful, come to us— he who,
bounteous as the face of the dawn, discloses desirable treasures for the donor.
And you, O Son of Strength, may you turn the gods toward us today at this sacrifice. May I ever abide in your bounty; may I, O Agni, be rich in heroes through your protection.
And may those two Nāsatyas come to my invocation; O wise ones, you are indeed inspired by our prayers.
Just as you delivered Atri from the great darkness, O heroes, rescue us from distress in the hour of need.

O gods, be you givers to us of wealth that is brilliant, full of vigor, rich in heroes, and abundant in food. Being gracious—whether celestial, terrestrial, born of the cow, or of the waters—be merciful to us, O gods.
May Rudra, Sarasvatī, Viṣṇu, and Vāyu, being of one mind and bounteous, be gracious to us;
may Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, the divine Ordainer, Parjanya, and Vāta cause our nourishment to swell.
And may that god Savitṛ, Bhaga, and Apāṃ Napāt, who bestows gifts, protect us;
may Tvaṣṭṛ, in harmony with the gods and their wives, and Dyaus with the gods, and Pṛthivī with the oceans, [protect us].
And may Ahi Budhnya hear us, and Aja Ekapād, Earth, and Ocean;
may all the gods, the increasers of *ṛta*, being invoked, and the hymns praised by sages, protect us.
Thus, O grandsons of mine, the Bharadvājas praise you with prayers and hymns;
you who have been invoked as the Gnas, the unassailable Vasus, you who are all worthy of worship and have been lauded.
Up rises that great eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, the beloved and undeceivable, the pure and beautiful face of Eternal Order (Ṛta). Like a golden ornament, it has shone forth at the rising of heaven.
The inspired sage who knows the three assemblies of these gods and their origin from of old—
he, the Sun, beholding both the straight and the crooked among mortals, surveys the ways of the noble.
I praise you, the guardians of the great cosmic order—Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, the well-born; Aryaman and Bhaga, whose thoughts are undeceived. I call upon these purifying ones who dwell together.

I approach with reverence the Ādityas and Aditi— the destroyers of enemies, the lords of the good, the undeceived, the great kings who bestow fair dwellings, the youthful rulers of heaven, the men of noble dominion.
O Father Heaven, O guileless Mother Earth, O Brother Agni, O Vasus, have mercy on us!
O all you Ādityas and Aditi, being of one accord, extend to us manifold protection.

O worshipful ones, do not deliver us over to the wolf, nor to the she-wolf, nor to any who intends us evil; for you are the charioteers of our bodies, and you have become the masters of our skill and our speech.
May we not suffer for the sin committed by another; O Vasus, may we not do that which you punish.
For you, O All-Gods, are the lords of all; may the enemy himself bring harm upon his own body.
Homage indeed to the fierce one; I seek to win favor with homage. Homage has supported the earth and the sky.
Homage to the gods; homage is their lord. Even a committed sin I seek to expiate through homage.

You who are the charioteers of Truth, whose will is purified, who dwell in the home of Truth, and who are undeceivable—to you, those far-seeing heroes, I bow with prostrations; I bow down before all of you, O great ones worthy of sacrifice.
For they possess the most excellent luster; they lead us across all difficulties.
Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—those of noble dominion, whose thoughts are fixed on the *ṛta*, who are kings of speech and devoted to truth.
May Indra, Earth, Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi, and the five peoples increase our strength;
may they be for us providers of good shelter, good protection, and good guidance, excellent saviors and good guardians.
Now may the divine assembly come; the Hotṛ, Bhāradvāja, seeks their favor.
With the sacrificial foods placed before him, the worshipper, seeking wealth, has paid homage to the race of the gods.
Drive away that crooked enemy, O Agni, the thief of evil intent; O Lord of the Good, make his path far distant and provide us with a way of easy passage.
O pressing-stones, O Soma, you have indeed yearned for us for the sake of friendship.
Strike down the greedy Paṇi, for he is a wolf.
For you indeed, O bounteous ones, with Indra as your chief, are directed toward heaven; make our path easy to travel on our journey, and be our guardians at home.
We have indeed entered upon the path that leads to well-being and is free from danger,
by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth.
I do not approve of that, whether by day or on earth, nor by sacrifice, nor by these ritual labors.
May the well-founded mountains crush him; may the performer of excessive sacrifice be brought low.

O Maruts, whoever holds us in contempt, or whoever seeks to find fault with the sacred prayer (*brahman*) being performed—may burning pains be his lot for his wicked deeds; may the heavens scorch that hater of sacred prayer.

Why indeed, O Soma, do they call you the guardian of the sacred word (*brahman*), and why indeed do they call you our protector against curses? Why indeed do you look with indifference upon us being reviled? Cast your burning weapon at the hater of the sacred word!
May the dawns as they are born protect me; may the swelling rivers protect me;
may the firm mountains protect me; and may the ancestors protect me at the invocation of the gods.
May we always be of good mind; may we indeed behold the rising sun.
May the Lord of treasures grant this, he who honors the gods and is most swift to come with his aid.
May Indra come most near with his protection; may Sarasvatī, swelling with the rivers, Parjanya, bringing delight with the herbs, and Agni—well-praised and easy to invoke—come like a father.
O All-Gods, come hither; hear this my invocation.
Sit down upon this sacred grass.
O gods, whoever honors you with an offering dripping with clarified butter—
to him do you all go.
May the sons of immortality hear our songs; may they be gracious toward us.
May all the gods, who increase the cosmic order and hear our invocation according to the seasons,
enjoy the appropriate milk.
May Indra with his host of Maruts, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, and Aryaman enjoy this hymn and these our oblations.
O Agni, as the Hotṛ-priest, perform this sacrifice of ours according to the sacred ordinances, you who are wise regarding the divine host.
O All-Gods, hear this my invocation—you who are in the intermediate space and you who dwell in heaven;
you who have Agni as your tongue, or you who are worthy of sacrifice—having seated yourselves upon this sacred grass, rejoice!
May all the gods worthy of sacrifice hear my prayer, as well as both the worlds and the Son of the Waters.
Let me not utter words that should be disregarded by you; may we rejoice most intimately within your favor.
Whosoever, great and possessing the power of the serpent, were born upon the earth, from heaven, or in the gathering place of the waters—
may those gods grant us all life for our sustenance, bestowing wide space through nights and dawns.
O Agni and Parjanya, you who are easy to invoke, favor my prayer at this invocation and our beautiful hymn of praise.
May one of you generate the sacrificial food (*iḷā*) and the other the embryo; bestow upon us nourishments that bring forth progeny.
Upon the strewn sacrificial grass, while the fire is kindled, I worship you with a hymn and great reverence.
O all you gods worthy of sacrifice, rejoice today in this oblation at our assembly.
O Pūṣan, Lord of the Path, we have yoked you for our prayer, as one yokes a chariot for the winning of spoil.
Bring to us manly wealth, a hero who bestows sacrificial gifts,
and a desirable master of the household.
O glowing Pūṣan, urge even the one who does not wish to give toward giving; soften even the mind of the niggard.
Clear the paths for the winning of booty; strike down the adversaries.
O Mighty One, may our prayers be successful.
O Sage, pierce through the hearts of the Paṇis with your iron spike;
then subject them to our will.
O Pūṣan, pierce with your goad; seek what is dear in the heart of the miser, and then deliver him over to us.
O Sage, tear asunder and rend the hearts of the Paṇis;
then deliver them over to us.
O Pūṣan,
O glowing one, with that goad which you carry as an inciter of prayer, scratch out the heart of this man and tear it to pieces.
O glowing one, that goad of yours which has horns of cattle and brings success to the herd—
of that we seek your favor.
And make our prayer win cattle, win horses, and win booty; make it like a man for our enjoyment.
O Pūṣan, lead us together with one who knows, who shall directly instruct us and say, "This indeed is it."
May we go together with Pūṣan, who shall point out the houses, saying, "These indeed are they."
The wheel of Pūṣan is not damaged; the axle-box does not fall away;
nor does its rim waver.
Whoever serves him with an oblation, Pūṣan does not neglect him;
he is the first to find wealth.
May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may Pūṣan protect our horses;
may Pūṣan win booty for us.
O Pūṣan, follow after the cows of the sacrificer who presses the soma,
and also those of us who offer praise.
Let none perish, let none be harmed, let none be shattered in a pit; then come hither with those who are unharmed.
We pray to Pūṣan, who hears us, the watchful one whose wealth is never lost,
the lord of riches.
O Pūṣan, under your protection may we never suffer harm;
we here are your praisers.
May Pūṣan place his right hand around us from beyond; may he bring back to us what we have lost.
Come, O Son of Deliverance, O Radiant One, let us two be united;
be the charioteer of our *ṛta*.
We implore the best of charioteers, the one with matted hair, the lord of great wealth, the friend of riches.
O glowing one, you are a stream of wealth; O Lord whose horses are goats, you are a mass of riches, the friend of every man who meditates upon you.
Now let us praise Pūṣan, the possessor of swift horses, who is drawn by goats,
he who is called the lover of his sister.
I have spoken to the suitor for my mother; may the lover of my sister hear us—my brother, the friend of Indra.
May the goats, firmly mounted upon the chariot, carry Pūṣan— the god who brings glory to the people— bearing him along.
Whoever accuses Pūṣan, saying,
"He ate the *karambha*," that person does not succeed in accusing the god.
And indeed, he, the best of charioteers, the lord of the good, joined with his friend as an ally,
Indra smites the Vṛtras.
And there, upon the speckled ox, the best of charioteers set down the golden wheel of the sun.
O Wondrous One, most wise, whatever we may say to you today, O much-praised one,
do you successfully accomplish that prayer of ours.
And may you lead this company of ours to the winning of cattle;
O Pūṣan, you are renowned from afar.
We pray for your blessing, which drives away evil and brings near prosperity; for well-being today in its fullness, and for well-being tomorrow in its fullness.
O Indra and Pūṣan, let us now invoke you for friendship, for well-being, and for the winning of booty.
One has approached the Soma pressed in the ladles to drink;
the other desires the groats.
Goats are the draft-animals of one; two bay steeds are harnessed to the other.
With those two, he strikes down the Vṛtras.
When Indra, the most virile, led forth the great waters according to the sacred law,
Pūṣan was there by his side.
Like a branch from the top of a tree, we grasp that benevolent favor of Pūṣan and of Indra.
We draw Pūṣan toward us, as a charioteer draws the reins;
and Indra for my great well-being.
One of your forms is bright, the other is worthy of sacrifice; like the sky, you possess two days of different colors.
For you, O self-dependent one, protect all wondrous powers. O Pūṣan, may your bounty here be auspicious.

With goats for steeds, guardian of cattle, whose home is strength, who quickens the prayer, and is established throughout all the world— Pūṣan, brandishing his supple goad, moves as a god surveying all created beings.
O Pūṣan, those golden ships of yours that travel within the ocean and through the intermediate space—
with those you go on a mission as the messenger of Sūrya, seeking glory and impelled by desire.
Pūṣan is the close kinsman from heaven and earth, the lord of nourishment, the bountiful one of wondrous luster—
he whom the gods gave to Sūryā, the strong and swift-moving one, created by desire.
Now, while the juices are being pressed, I shall proclaim those heroic deeds which you two have performed:
your fathers, the enemies of the gods, have been slain; O Indra and Agni, you two remain alive.
Truly, O Indra and Agni, such is your greatness, most worthy of praise;
you have a common father, you are brothers, and here you have mothers who are twins.
Having settled together at the pressed juice like two horses yoked to a feast,
Indra and Agni, those wielders of the thunderbolt— those two gods we now invoke here for our protection.
O Indra and Agni, you who increase the cosmic order (*ṛtāvṛdhā*), when one praises you while these Soma juices are pressed—
O gods, you who consume the offerings of the *pajra* clan, do not disregard the words of him who speaks with devotion.
O Indra and Agni, what mortal man among you two gods understands this?
One of you, yoking his horses that move in different directions, speeds along on a common chariot.
O Indra and Agni, this footless one has come before those with feet; casting aside her head, moving while speaking loudly with her tongue, she has stepped down thirty paces.
O Indra and Agni, for men stretch their bows with their arms;
do not abandon us in this great contest for wealth, in the pursuits for cattle.
O Indra and Agni, the hostilities of the enemy and his ill-will torment me; drive away those who hate us and keep them far from the light of the sun.
O Indra and Agni, yours are the treasures of heaven and of earth;
bestow upon us here wealth that nourishes all our life.
O Indra and Agni, you who are borne by hymns, who hear our invocation through our praises—
come with all our songs for the drinking of this Soma.
He pierces Vṛtra and wins the prize—whoever shall worship Indra and Agni, the two conquerors;
they who rule over abundant wealth, most powerful with their might, and striving for victory.
O Indra and Agni, fight now for those cows, the waters, the sun, and the stolen dawns;
O Indra, you take possession of the quarters, the sun, and the bright dawns; O Agni, drawn by your team of horses, you seize the waters and the cows.
O slayers of Vṛtra, come hither with your Vṛtra-slaying strengths, O Indra and Agni, through our prostrations. O Indra and Agni, with your ungrudging and most excellent gifts, be present with us.
I invoke those two by whom all this that was done of old has been accomplished;
Indra and Agni do not disregard us.
We invoke Indra and Agni, the fierce ones who strike down the adversaries; may they be gracious to us in such a plight.
The two lords of the virtuous have slain the Āryan enemies; they have slain the Dāsa enemies;
they have slain all our foes.
O Indra and Agni, these hymns of praise have resounded toward you both; drink the pressed juice, O you who bring auspiciousness!
O Heroes, Indra and Agni, with those many-desired teams of horses which you possess for the donor, come hither!
With those [horses], O heroes, come hither to this pressed libation,
O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
Praise him who with his flame embraces all the forests;
he makes them black with his tongue.
The mortal who, having kindled [the fire], seeks to win the favor of Indra, crosses the waters easily for the sake of glory.
Grant us food accompanied by vigor and swift horses,
so that we may carry Indra and Agni [to the sacrifice].
I invoke you both, O Indra and Agni; may you both together rejoice in the sacrificial gift.
You both are givers of food and riches; I call upon you both for the winning of strength.
Come to us with wealth in cattle, in horses, and in riches;
we invoke those two gods, Indra and Agni, the friends who bring auspiciousness for our friendship.
O Indra and Agni, hear the call of the sacrificer who presses the soma; enjoy the offerings, come hither, and drink the sweet soma.
This [Sarasvatī] bestowed the impetuous Divodāsa, the remover of debt, upon Vadhryaśva who gave oblations;
she who has devoured the Paṇi who consumed every abundance—those are thy mighty gifts, O Sarasvatī.
With her surging billows, she has shattered the ridges of the mountains like one digging for lotus-stalks;
with well-fashioned hymns and inspired thoughts, let us invoke Sarasvatī—the slayer of Pārāvata—for our protection.
O Sarasvatī, strike down those who revile the gods; destroy the progeny of every deceitful Bṛsaya.
Furthermore, you found the waters for the people; O possessor of plenty, you caused the poison to flow away from them.
May the goddess Sarasvatī, rich in spoils, protect us with her strengths; may she, the guardian of inspired thoughts, aid us.
O Goddess Sarasvatī, whoever invokes you when the prize is at stake,
as one calls upon Indra in the struggle against Vṛtra.
O Goddess Sarasvatī, you who are swift in the contests for booty, protect us; like Pūṣan, grant us a gain.
And may Sarasvatī, the terrible one whose path is golden, the slayer of Vṛtra, desire our fair praise.
She whose ocean is infinite, unassailable, brilliant, and ever-moving— she moves about, roaring with might.
May she, the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*), carry us across all hostilities and her other sister-rivers,
just as the sun stretches across the sky.
And may Sarasvatī, who is dear among the dear, who has seven sisters, and who is well-beloved, be worthy of our praise.
Having filled the earthly realms, the wide expanse, and the intermediate space, may Sarasvatī protect us from those who revile us.
Abiding in three places, consisting of seven parts, increasing the five races—
may she be worthy of invocation in every contest for booty.

She who is distinguished by her greatness among the great, surpassing others in splendor as the most active of the active; like a vast chariot fashioned for power, Sarasvatī is to be praised by the wise.
O Sarasvatī, lead us toward greater wealth; do not shrink away from us, nor fail us with your milk.
Accept our friendship and our household service; may we never go from you to desolate lands.

I praise the two heroes who are the masters of this heaven; chanting with hymns, I invoke the Aśvins, those who at the breaking of dawn instantly strive to reach the ends of the earth and the wide expanses.
Advancing to the sacrifice with their pure [rays], they have illuminated the splendor of the chariot through the mists;
measuring out many immeasurable spaces, you two pass over the waters, the deserts, and the plains.
O ye two fierce ones, you have indeed repeatedly brought that path which is not to be obstructed, with your steeds swift as thought,
impetuous, and eager to rest, in order to bypass the distress of the mortal who offers oblations.

Let the ancient, guileless Hotṛ worship the two youthful ones who have harnessed their steeds, who attend to the prayer of the one who praises them anew, and who bring splendor, nourishment, food, and strength.

I invoke with a new hymn those two who are beautiful, wondrous, and most helpful to many— the ancient ones who have become the greatest bestowers of bliss to him who recites and praises, granting manifold gifts to the singer.
With your winged steeds, you carried Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, out from the waters, from the ocean, through the mid-air;
traversing dustless leagues with your feathered horses, you brought him forth from the lap of the billowing sea.
O victorious chariot-borne ones, you shattered the mountain; O bulls, you heard the call of Vadhrimatī.
Bestowing favor upon Śayu, you made the cow swell with milk; thus, O swift and active ones, you brought about the grace of Cyavāna.
Whatever wrath of the gods or among mortals has existed from of old throughout heaven and earth—
that, O Ādityas, Vasus, and Rudriyas, bestow as burning evil upon him who is joined with the Rākṣasas.
May he who ordains Mitra and Varuṇa, the two kings, according to the seasons, perceive this [prayer] across the mid-air;
let him hurl his weapon at the deep-seated demon and at the deceitful speech of the enemy.
With your inner wheels, come on your glorious, hero-bearing chariot to provide a path for our offspring.
With your secret weapon and the abandonment of the mortal, strike off the heads of those who would attack us.
Come hither with your teams of horses— the highest, the midmost, and the lowest—
to open the doors of even the firm cow-stall for the singer, O you of wondrous bounty.

Where has the reverent hymn of praise found those two beautiful ones today, who are invoked by many, like a messenger? O Nāsatyas, he has turned you hither, for you are most dear to this man’s prayer.
Come readily to this my invocation, being praised so that you may drink the soma-juice;
go around that path of yours which no foe, whether far or near, can overcome.
The soma-juice has been prepared for you in the wide space; the sacrificial grass has been spread out, most easy to traverse.
With uplifted hands, seeking you both, the worshipper has paid homage; the pressing-stones, approaching, have adorned you.
Upright has Agni stood for you at the sacrifices; forth goes the gift, the glowing ladle full of clarified butter.
The Hotṛ-priest, joyfully minded, choosing [the gods], has yoked those who are the Nāsatyas when he calls upon them with oblations.
For the sake of glory, the daughter of Sūrya mounted the chariot, O you of many enjoyments, for a hundredfold protection.
By means of your wondrous powers, you two became masters of illusion here, O heroes, dancers at the birth of those worthy of sacrifice.
With these visible splendors, you two brought forth prosperity for Sūryā’s wedding;
birds flew after you for the sake of your wondrous form, and a well-praised song reached you, O ye worthy of devotion.
O Nāsatyas, may your birds and horses, the best at carrying, bring you toward the offerings;
let your chariot, swift as thought, be sent forth toward the many nourishments and strengthening foods.
For many indeed are the gifts for you two, O you who enjoy much; make our nourishment swell like a cow, inexhaustible.
And let both praise and fair hymn be for you, O lovers of sweetness, and let the juices follow your bounty.
Moreover, two swift, ruddy mares of Puraya, a hundred cooked portions at Sumīḷha,
and for Peruka— Śāṇḍa gave ten golden, well-disposed, high-standing, submissive stallions as attendants.
O Nāsatyas, may he who has many paths grant you hundreds and thousands of horses for our song;
O heroes, may he now grant them to the singer Bharadvāja. May the two of you, performers of many wonders, slay the Rākṣasas. May they be [our protectors].
May we, together with the patrons, abide in your favor within the wide expanse.
The Dawns have risen up, radiant with splendor, like bright waves of water.
She makes all paths easy to travel and well-prepared; the noble gift of the wealthy patron has become manifest.
Auspicious, you have been seen; you shine far and wide. Your flames and rays have flown up to heaven.
Adorning yourself, you reveal your breast, O Goddess Dawn, shining with great splendors.
The ruddy, gleaming oxen carry her forth, the fortunate one who spreads out widely.
She drives away the darkness like a hero against his enemies; she repels it like a swift chariot-horse.
O well-guided one, you travel by easy paths over the mountains; O self-radiant one, you cross the waters even where there is no wind.
O daughter of heaven, bring us wealth upon your broad path, O exalted one, so that we may have nourishment.
O Dawn, bring us wealth with your yoked horses; you carry the boon according to our desire.
O Daughter of Heaven, you who are a goddess, you have become beautiful through your greatness at the first invocation.
Even the birds have flown up from their dwellings at your dawning, as have the men who partake of food.
To the mortal who dwells at home and offers gifts, O Goddess Dawn, you bring abundant wealth.
This daughter of heaven, born of the sky, awakening the human settlements, has stirred them up;
she who, with her radiant glow, has become manifest through the nights even across the darkness.
They have gone forth with their ruddy-yoked horses; the Dawns, with their shining chariots, gleam brilliantly. Leading the vanguard of the great sacrifice, they drive away the darkness of the night.
Bringing renown, booty, nourishment, and strength to the mortal who offers oblations, O wealthy Dawns,
ruling over a realm rich in heroes, bestow protection today and grant treasure to the one who honors you.
For now, O Dawns, you possess treasure for the one who honors you; now, for the heroic man who offers oblations;
now, for the inspired singer who chants his hymns. You have indeed brought it even to one like me, as you did in former times.
For now, O Dawn, you whose back is the mountain, the Aṅgirases sing to you for the sake of the cow-pens;
with song and with prayer they have burst them open, and the invocation of the gods by men has become effective.
Shine forth for us from heaven as of old, O daughter of Heaven, O generous one, for the one who serves you like Bharadvāja.
Bestow upon the singer wealth with noble heroes; grant us far-reaching renown.
That form of hers must indeed be a marvel even to one who understands, she who bears the common name of "Cow.
While one [aspect] swells among mortals for milking, the speckled one has once yielded her bright udder.
Those who, like kindled fires, have shone forth when the Maruts grew strong— twice and thrice—
their chariots became dustless and golden, together with their manly vigor and heroic powers.

Those who are the sons of the bounteous Rudra, whom the steadfast one must now bring forth—the Great Mother, she the vast one, has indeed known them; that Pr̥śni has conceived the germ for the noble one.

They who do not shrink from their birth, purifying themselves even while remaining within the impurities; when the pure ones have milked forth [the Soma] according to their pleasure, they sprinkle their own bodies with splendor.
Swift indeed are they, by whom even this bold Marut host was brought near, bearing their names;
they who are not stingy, who are tireless in their greatness—may the bounteous one never fail those fierce ones.
These fierce ones, with their power and bold armies, have yoked both well-established worlds;
then indeed, Rodasī, shining by herself, has stood among them as she does among the clouds, like a light.
By this [chariot] may your journey be, O Maruts—one that even without horses and without a charioteer drives it;
needing no support and having no reins, crossing the mid-air, it goes straight through the two worlds along its path.
O Maruts, there is no one who can hinder or overcome him whom you protect in the struggle for booty;
he who wins offspring, cattle, progeny, and waters—he shall burst open the enclosure on the decisive day of battle.
Offer a brilliant hymn to the singing, swift Marut host, who possesses their own inherent power—those who by force overcome all forces; O Agni, the earth trembles before these mighty ones.
Radiant like the flash of a sacrifice, like the eager tongues of Agni,
the Maruts— praising, roaring like heroes, born in splendor— are invincible.
I invite with my invocation that growing host of Maruts, whose spears are flashing, the sons of Rudra;
for the host of heaven, the pure prayers have contended like fierce waters from the mountains.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may I magnify you with songs—you who are the most eminent among all existing beings;
you two who, like reins, most effectively restrain and guide the two unequalled peoples with your own arms.
This prayer of mine is spread out for you both; may it reach the dear sacred grass with our homage.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, grant us an unassailable shelter, that which is your protective refuge, O bounteous givers.
Come hither, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with fair praise, being invoked with dear homage! You two, who bestow wealth upon men like workers, restrain even those who seek to hear you by your greatness.
Like spirited horses, they whose kin are purified, when Aditi bore the embryo according to the *ṛta*;
they who, being great and mighty at birth, have established themselves as terrible for the sake of the mortal enemy.
When all the gods, rejoicing in their greatness and being of one accord, bestowed sovereign power upon you both; when you encompass even the two wide worlds, your spies are undeceived and unerring.
For you two maintain sovereign power day after day; you make firm the ridge as if from the highest heaven.
Firm is the constellation, belonging to all the gods; it has stretched out the earth and the sky with its nourishing stream.
You two sustain the body so that it may fill the belly, when the offerings together fill the sacrificial seat.
The young women do not fail; when they, who invigorate all, bring forth the milk in abundance.
May the wise one ever approach you both with his tongue, since the true steward has appeared according to the *ṛta*.
O you whose food is ghee, let that be your greatness; may you two drive away the distress of the donor.

When those who strive against you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, violate your dear ordinances established by you— those who are neither gods through their power nor mortals, yet associate with the unrighteous, like sons of the waters.
When the singers bring forth their speech and some recite the *nivid* formulas with devotion, then we shall proclaim true hymns to you both; for in your greatness, you are not restrained by the gods.
Truly, under your protection, O Mitra and Varuṇa, your shelter is close at hand and not far off,
when the cows follow the straight-flying, bold, and vigorous bull as he speeds forth in battle.
With eager hearing, the sacrifice is raised for you both; may he who has spread the sacrificial grass, like Manu, worship you in unison.
O Indra and Varuṇa, may he turn hither today for great refreshment and for great favor.

For they are indeed the best at the gathering of the gods, the most impetuous and strongest among heroes; for they have become the most generous of the wealthy patrons, possessing great vigor, overcoming Vṛtra by the Eternal Law (Ṛta), and accompanied by all their armies.
Praise them with reverent hymns and invocations, O Indra and Varuṇa, who are eager for our well-being:
one of you, by his might, strikes Vṛtra with the thunderbolt; the other, the sage, attends to the assemblies.
When all the wives and men have grown strong, and all the gods, self-praised among men;
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two have surpassed them in greatness—O Heaven and Earth, you two have become wide.
He indeed is the bountiful giver, possessing good horses and upholding the *ṛta*, who worships you two, O Indra and Varuṇa, with his own self.
May that liberal man cross over his enemies by means of nourishment; may he win wealth and [the favor of] men who possess riches.

O Gods, Indra and Varuṇa, that wealth which you bestow upon the performer of the sacrifice—abounding in goods and rich in cattle—may it be ours; may it be that which shatters the curses of our adversaries.
And may there be for us, O Indra and Varuṇa, wealth for our patrons— wealth protected by gods and well-guarded—
those whose vigor triumphs in battles, and who, as swift conquerors, immediately extend their splendors.

Now, O gods Indra and Varuṇa, being praised, bestow wealth upon us for the sake of glorious renown. Thus praising the host of the Mighty One, may we cross over difficulties as if crossing waters by boat.
Sing forth now a beloved hymn, wide-reaching, to the sovereign Varuṇa, the great god;
he who by his majesty governs the two wide worlds, whose vows are mighty, and who shines with wisdom like one undecaying with his flame.

O Indra and Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed juice, you who uphold the sacred law, drink this pressed Soma, the intoxicating draught. Your chariot comes toward the sacrifice for the feast of the gods, to the dwelling place, for the drinking.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two bulls, drink of this most honeyed, potent Soma. This juice has been poured out for you among us; having sat down upon this sacred grass (barhis), may you both rejoice.

I urge you both together with this rite and with food, O Indra and Viṣṇu, at the completion of this work. May you enjoy the sacrifice and bestow wealth upon us, carrying us across by paths that are free from harm.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, you who are the progenitors of all thoughts and the vessels that hold the Soma;
may our recited hymns favor you, and may our praises sung with chants be pleasing to you.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, lords of the exhilarating draughts, come to the Soma, bestowing wealth;
let the ointments of our prayers anoint you both, and let the hymns being recited with their lauds join together.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, may your horses, the subduers of enemies, bring you to our common feast;
may you both graciously accept all the invocations of our thoughts, and listen to my prayers and songs.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, that deed of yours is worthy of praise: in the exhilaration of Soma, you have made wide space; you have made the mid-region broader and have spread out the realms for our life.

O Indra and Viṣṇu, being strengthened by the oblation, having received the first portion through our homage, and having been presented with the offerings—drinking the clarified butter, bestow wealth upon us; you two are the ocean, the vessel that holds the Soma.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, drink of this sweet Soma; O wonder-workers, fill your bellies with it. The intoxicating juices have come to you; listen to my prayers and hear my call.
Both of you have conquered; you are not defeated, nor has either one of you been defeated. O Indra and Viṣṇu, when you two strove together, you divided the thousandfold [booty] into three parts.

Rich in clarified butter, the support of all beings, wide and broad, yielding honey and well-adorned— Heaven and Earth, by the ordinance of Varuṇa, are held apart, ageless and overflowing with abundant seed.
Unfailing, with many streams, rich in milk, they yield clarified butter for the doer of good deeds, O you of pure vows.
You two, Rodasī, who rule over this world, pour upon us that seed which was established by Manu.
O Heaven and Earth, O two Dhiṣaṇās, that mortal who offers worship to you both for the sake of upright conduct prospers;
he is multiplied with offspring according to the sacred law, as diverse forms of like nature are poured forth from you.
Heaven and Earth are enveloped in ghee; they are adorned with ghee, filled with ghee, and increased by ghee.
Vast and wide, established as the chief priests for the choosing of the Hotṛ, them indeed the sages praise for the sake of obtaining favor and for their sacrifice.
May Heaven and Earth bestow sweetness upon us—those who drip sweetness, who yield sweetness, whose laws are sweet;
they who, as deities, establish the sacrifice and wealth for us, granting great renown, booty, and heroic strength.

May both Heaven and Earth swell nourishment for us—the Father and Mother, all-knowing and of wondrous deeds. May the two world-halves, harmonious and bringing welfare to all, together bestow upon us gain, strength, and wealth.
Upward has this god Savitṛ, the wise one, extended his golden arms for the sake of the pressing.
He, the liberal, the young, the very skillful, sprinkles his hands with ghee in the supporting expanse of the mid-air.
May we abide under the impulse of the god Savitṛ, for the bestowal of the most excellent wealth—
he who is the master of all bipeds and quadrupeds, both in their resting place and in their movement throughout the world.
O Savitṛ, with your undeceivable and auspicious guardians, protect our household today.
O golden-tongued one, guard us for the sake of new prosperity; let no malevolent speaker have power over us.
Up has risen this god Savitṛ, the friend of the home, golden-handed, at the arrival of evening.
With iron jaws, holy, and sweet-tongued, he bestows abundant wealth upon the donor.
Like a priest, Savitar has raised his golden arms, he of the beautiful countenance.
He has ascended the heights of heaven and the earth; he has brought to rest whatever beast flies about.
O Savitṛ, grant us what is auspicious today, and what is auspicious tomorrow, and what is auspicious day by day;
for through this prayer, O God, may we be partakers of an auspicious and abundant dwelling.
O Indra and Soma, great indeed is that majesty of yours; you two performed the first great deeds.
You two found the sun and you found the light; you struck away all darkness and reproaches.
O Indra and Soma, you cause Uṣas to dwell; you lead forth the sun together with its light.
You propped up the sky with a support and spread out the earth, the mother, far and wide.
O Indra and Soma, you slew the dragon Vṛtra who obstructed the waters; the heaven approved of your deed.
You set free the channels of the rivers and filled the many oceans.
O Indra and Soma, you placed the cooked [milk] within the raw bellies of the cows;
you seized it within these bright, variegated moving creatures, even though it was not yet bound.
O Indra and Soma, you two indeed have bestowed a victorious, renowned, and glorious offspring;
you two, O fierce ones, have extended manly strength to the people, a power that overcomes hostile armies.

Bṛhaspati, the breaker of the rock, the first-born, the follower of Truth, the descendant of Aṅgiras, accompanied by oblations; he who dwells in the two worlds, who sits at the *pragharma* sacrifice, our father, the bull—roars aloud.

Bṛhaspati, who has created wide space even for such people as these at the invocation of the gods—he, slaying the Vṛtras, shatters the fortresses; conquering his enemies and foes, he prevails in the battles.
Bṛhaspati has won all treasures; this god has captured the great pens of cattle.
Desiring to win the waters and the light, the irresistible Bṛhaspati slays the enemy with his hymns.

O Soma and Rudra, maintain your divine power; may our offerings reach you swiftly. Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, be auspicious to us—be a blessing to our bipeds and a blessing to our quadrupeds.
O Soma and Rudra, tear away in all directions the disease that has entered our home.
Drive Nirṛti far away; may auspicious glories attend us.
O Soma and Rudra, bestow all these healing remedies upon our bodies.
Untie and release from us whatever sin has been committed that is bound within our bodies.
O Soma and Rudra, wielders of sharp weapons and sharp missiles, who are most gracious—be merciful to us here!
Release us from the noose of Varuṇa and protect us with well-disposed minds.
Like the appearance of a rain-cloud is his countenance when, clad in armor, he goes into the lap of the battle-arrays.
With an uninjured body, may you be victorious; may the greatness of this armor protect you.
With the bow may we win cattle, with the bow may we win the battle; with the bow may we conquer fierce encounters.
The bow turns the enemy's will away; with the bow may we conquer all the quarters.
As if about to speak, she comes close to the ear, embracing her dear friend;
like a woman, this bowstring twangs upon the stretched bow, carrying us across in the encounter.
Moving together like a young woman to her lover, may they bear [the arrow] in their lap like a mother her son;
may these two bow-ends, acting in concert and quivering, pierce the enemies and strike down the foes.
The father of many, he has many sons; having entered the fray, he makes a whizzing sound.
With the quiver bound upon his back, urged forward, he conquers all encounters and all hostile armies.
Standing on the chariot, the skillful charioteer leads the spirited horses forward wherever he desires.
Admire the greatness of the reins; from behind, the traces follow the will of the mind.
Making loud noises, the horses with strong hooves, striving for prize-winning strength together with their chariots,
trampling the enemies with their forefeet, destroy the foes without retreating.
The chariot-stand is his oblation, and there his weapon and his armor are laid;
there may we ever sit upon the strong chariot, being well-disposed in spirit.
The Fathers, who sit at the sweet draught, bestowers of vital strength, who have endured hardships, powerful, profound,
possessing wondrous armies and the force of arrows, tireless, truly heroic, vast, and conquerors of hosts.
O Brahmins, O Fathers, worthy of Soma; may Heaven and Earth, the auspicious and faultless, be gracious to us.
May Pūṣan protect us from misfortune, O increasers of Truth; guard us, and let no one who speaks evil have power over us.
She wears beautiful feathers; her tooth is of deer-horn; bound with cow-hide, she flies forth when loosed.
Where men run together and apart, there may the arrows grant us protection.
O *ṛjīti*, spare us; let our bodies be as stone.
May Soma speak for us, and may Aditi grant us protection.
They strike their backs; they beat upon their haunches. O wise horse-whip, urge the horses on in the battles!
Like a serpent with its coils, he encircles the arm, warding off the stroke of the bowstring; the hand-guard, knowing all the ways, as a man, shall protect the man from every side.
Coated with poison, with the head of a deer, and having iron for its mouth—
this great bow to the divine Arrow, whose seed is Parjanya, receives our profound homage.
Loosed, fly away, O arrow, sharpened by prayer!
Go to the enemies; fall upon them, and leave not a single one of them remaining.
Where the arrows fly together like boys with shorn hair—there may Brahmaṇaspati and Aditi grant us protection; may they grant us protection for all days.
I cover your vital organs with armor; may King Soma clothe you with immortality.
May Varuṇa make for you a space wider than the wide; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer.
Whoever—whether our own kin, a stranger, or one dwelling afar—seeks to strike us down, may all the gods destroy him; may the sacred word (*brahman*) be my inner armor.
